section.heading: 2. MOS 2110, Ordnance Vehicle Maintenance Officer (III) (CWO5 to WO) PMOS,

provision.text: MOS 2110, Ordnance Vehicle Maintenance Officer (III) (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DC I&L

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Ordnance Vehicle Maintenance Officers manage the equipment readiness, work progress, and maintenance personnel qualification/training. They manage the activities of personnel engaged in the recovery, salvage, and maintenance of weapon systems (ordnance vehicles). They supervise the functional areas of maintenance management, establish field maintenance sites, and procedures for the defense of those sites. They manage command environmental hazardous waste programs, and supervise and provide oversight of disposal, storage, emergency planning for hazardous waste, and ozone depleting substances.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
This MOS may only be assigned to WOs previously qualified in MOSs 2141, 2146, 2147, or 2149.
Must meet eligibility and appointment criteria as prescribed in MCO 1040.42B, WO and LDO accession programs.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements
Complete the Ground Ordnance Maintenance Officer Course (A14RGZ6) at U.S. Army Ordnance Center and School, Ft Gregg-Adams, VA.
Complete the Warrant Officer Basic Course (WOBC) (M02RMN4), The Basic School, Quantico, VA within 18 months of appointment to WO. 1116 NAVMC 1200.1L

section.heading: 3. MOS 2120, Ground Ordnance Maintenance Officer (III) (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DC

provision.text: MOS 2120, Ground Ordnance Maintenance Officer (III) (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DC I&L

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Ground Ordnance Maintenance Officers are special staff officers who manage ground ordnance equipment readiness, accountability and security. They serve as technical advisers on the appropriate employment of ground ordnance maintenance resources. They oversee the activities of personnel engaged in the recovery, salvage, and maintenance of weapons, fire control systems, artillery, fires platforms, optical and electro-optical/ laser devices, small missile and other manned, remote, or semi-autonomous ground ordnance systems. They nest maintenance support packages into their commander's mission requirements to enable mission accomplishment. They must possess skills in managing resources with an emphasis on efficient personnel employment, maintaining equipment readiness, and exercise/deployment planning. Ground Ordnance Maintenance Officers must possess a working knowledge of forecasting equipment readiness and availability, monitoring and managing maintenance requirements, and effectively advising commanders. They mentor the officers and Marines within their unit in all applicable physical, doctrinal, and conceptual maintenance operations to improve the effectiveness of the command. They also develop maintenance policy at various levels, and manage work progress and maintenance personnel qualification/training. They establish maintenance production lines, procedures for inspection, and quality assurance on repaired equipment. They supervise the functional areas of maintenance management and can supervise the storage, disposal, and emergency planning for hazardous waste and ozone depleting substances. They liaise with project managers and sustainment partners to address maintenance requirements and to advance enterprise ingenuity in expeditionary ground ordnance maintenance support and weapon system lethality. Additional duties will include participation in applicable course curriculum review boards (CCRB), curriculum development for new equipment, and review of draft ground ordnance maintenance training and readiness manuals. Warrant Officers and junior chief warrant officers generally serve in maintenance companies and battalion staffs. They progress to serve on regimental staffs within the ground combat element and within the command element and supporting establishment. At the most senior ranks, 2120s serve billets which provide the greatest breadth of influence and include Headquarters Marine Corps supporting activities that analyze, design, and develop standards-based training for individual and collective progression, as well as billets which support the requirements development and acquisition processes of ground ordnance systems and related maintenance support equipment. At this level, Ground Ordnance Maintenance Officers must also be able to supervise operational level maintenance, integrate maintenance support into major subordinate command, service, and joint operations, manage maintenance policy and doctrine, manage the training and education continuum for ground ordnance maintenance personnel and provide staff level planning and technical advice concerning maintenance capabilities and supportability for MAGTF commanders. 1116 NAVMC 1200.1L 1-102 Enclosure (1)

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Must have previously served in one of the following MOSs 2111, 2112, 2131, 2161, 2171, or 2181.
Must meet eligibility and appointment criteria as prescribed in MCO 1040.42B, WO and LDO accession programs.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements
Complete the Ground Ordnance Maintenance Officer Course (A14RGZ6) at U.S. Army Ordnance Center and School, Ft Gregg-Adams, VA.
Complete the Warrant Officer Basic Course (WOBC) (M02RMN4), The Basic School, Quantico, VA within 18 months of appointment to WO.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to reference (au), Ground Ordnance Maintenance Training and Readiness Manual.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code. First-Line Supervisors/Managers of Mechanics, Installers, and Repairers 49- 1011.

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Related Military Skill
Ordnance Officer, 2102.
Ordnance Vehicle Maintenance Officer, 2110. 1117 NAVMC 1200.1L 1-103 Enclosure (1) 1117. OCCUPATIONAL FIELD 23, AMMUNITION AND EXPLOSIVE ORDNANCE DISPOSAL

section.heading: 1. MOS 2305, Explosive Ordnance Disposal Officer (II/III) (LtCol to Capt)

provision.text: MOS 2305, Explosive Ordnance Disposal Officer (II/III) (LtCol to Capt) and (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DC I&L

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) Officers supervise command and control EOD operations and personnel. Additionally, they also serve as special staff officers. EOD Officers are responsible for the EOD function in support of the MAGTF, supporting establishments, homeland defense, and special operations forces by locating, accessing, identifying, rendering safe, neutralizing, and disposing of hazards, both foreign and domestic chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear, and high-yield explosive (CBRNE), unexploded explosive ordnance (UXO), improvised explosive device (IED), and weapons of mass destruction (WMD) that present a threat to operations, installations, personnel, or materiel.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Security requirement: top secret security clearance eligibility.
Must have normal color vision and no claustrophobic tendencies.
Only MOS 2305 WOs may apply for appointment as a MOS 2305 LDO.
Must meet eligibility and appointment criteria as prescribed in MCO 1040.42B, WO and LDO accession programs.
Must meet the medical requirements listed in article 15-107 per reference (ai) for explosive handling and/or explosive driver.

This MOS may only be assigned to WOs who served at least five years in the MOS 2336 having achieved, at a minimum, the Senior EOD Breast Insignia Qualification. This will be documented in a page 11 entry, and/or through MCTFS, and should also be documented within the command endorsement of the WO package and a letter of recommendation from a Marine Corps EOD Officer serving in an EOD Officer billet.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements
Complete the Explosive Ordnance Disposal Officer Course (M09B0E1), Twentynine Palms, CA.
Warrant Officers must complete the Warrant Officer Basic Course (WOBC) (M02RMN4) within 18 months of appointment.

Requirements for continued qualification and progression training all EOD officers will be annually screened for continued service in the EOD MOS using NAVMC form 11362. Based on the comprehensive standards covered under NAVMC form 11362, EOD Officers will not be screened using NAVMC form 11386.
The following core competencies must be trained to and sustained by all EOD Officers.

provision.label: (a)
provision.text: UXO operations.

provision.label: (b)
provision.text: WMD operations. 1117 NAVMC 1200.1L 1-104 Enclosure (1)

provision.label: (c)
provision.text: Advanced electronics.

provision.label: (d)
provision.text: IED defeat operations.

provision.label: (e)
provision.text: Post blast investigation.

provision.label: (f)
provision.text: Disassembly and inerting.

provision.label: (g)
provision.text: Explosive ordnance exploitation.

provision.label: (h)
provision.text: Specialized demolition techniques.

provision.label: (i)
provision.text: Destruction of explosive ordnance.

provision.label: (j)
provision.text: Explosive ordnance reconnaissance.

provision.label: (k)
provision.text: EOD robotics employment and usage.

provision.label: (l)
provision.text: Render safe of explosive ordnance (EO).

provision.label: (m)
provision.text: Advanced TTPs for EOD tools and equipment.

provision.label: (n)
provision.text: Homemade explosives (HME) identification and neutralization.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to reference (by), Explosive Ordnance Disposal Technician/Officer Training and Readiness Manual, and reference (ba), Marine Corps EOD Program.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code. Emergency Management Specialists 13-1061.

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Related Military Skill. None.

section.heading: 2. MOS 2339, Marine EOD Diver Officer (II/III) (LtCol to Capt) and (CWO5 to

provision.text: MOS 2339, Marine EOD Diver Officer (II/III) (LtCol to Capt) and (CWO5 to WO) NMOS (2305), DC I&L

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. A Marine EOD Officer who is trained to dive and use littoral explosive ordnance neutralization (LEON) equipment in the underwater environment. This title and MOS will also be used to identify Marine Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) Diver Officer Billets in the T/Os.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites. Must be a graduate of Naval School Explosive Ordnance Disposal (NAVSCOLEOD) (N56GPX1).

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements
Complete the MK 16 Underwater Breathing Apparatus (UBA) Diver Course (N20YC11) at the Naval Dive and Salvage Training Center, Panama City, FL.
Complete the Navy Scuba Diver Course (N2003E1) or the Navy Basic Scuba Diver Course (A-[contact withheld]) at the Naval Dive and Salvage Training Center, Panama City, FL.

Complete the EOD Basic Navy Underwater Course (N56B0Q1) at NAVSCOLEOD, Eglin AFB Florida or must complete the LEON MOJT program supervised by a Marine EOD Diver (MOS 2339). 1117 NAVMC 1200.1L 1-105 Enclosure (1)

Must maintain physically qualified per naval special warfare/ special operations physical to perform diver duties in accordance with inter- service requirements established in NAVMED P-117 and reference, standards of medical fitness.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties. (LtCol to Capt) and (CWO5 to WO): Plans, leads and employs Marine EOD LEON equipment; conducting underwater operations to detect, locate, reacquire, render safe/neutralize, recover, exploit, and dispose of underwater explosive ordnance in the very shallow water and surf zone.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code. Commercial Diver 49-9092.

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Related Military Skill. None.

section.heading: 3. MOS 2340, Ammunition Officer (II/III) (LtCol to Capt) and (CWO5 to WO)

provision.text: MOS 2340, Ammunition Officer (II/III) (LtCol to Capt) and (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, MCSC

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Ammunition Officers supervise and coordinate ammunition supply and renovation functions. These functions include, but are not limited to, procurement, receipt, storage, issue, handling, shipment, salvage, and renovation of ammunition. They also operate ammunition supply points and are responsible for the establishment of field ammunition supply points in forward areas. Ammunition Officers are assigned to billets on the general staff level and are responsible for advising those commanders on matters relating to the development of ammunition allowances for both training and combat operations. Assignments may also include commanding an ammunition company.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
2340 LDOs must achieve selection by the board.
Security requirement: secret security clearance eligibility.
This MOS may only be assigned to Warrant Officers who were previously qualified in MOS 2311.
Must meet eligibility and appointment criteria as prescribed in MCO 1040.42B, WO and LDO accession programs.

Only MOS 2340 warrant officers may apply for appointment as a MOS 2340 limited duty officer (LDO). Warrant Officers applying for MOS 2340 LDO must have demonstrated ammunition technical qualification through performance of duty as a warrant officer in ammunition billets.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements
Warrant Officers must complete the Warrant Officer Basic Course (WOBC) (M02RMN4) within 18 months of appointment.
Complete the Advanced Ammunition Operations Planner Course (A14GPY6), U.S. Army Ordnance Missile and Munitions Center and School, Ft Gregg-Adams, VA.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to reference (bz), Ammunition Technician/Officer Training and Readiness Manual. 1117 NAVMC 1200.1L 1-106 Enclosure (1)

provision.label: e.

provision.text: Related Military Skill. None. 1118 NAVMC 1200.1L 1-107 Enclosure (1) 1118. OCCUPATIONAL FIELD 26, SIGNALS INTELLIGENCE/ELECTRONIC WARFARE/ CYCBERSPACE OPERATIONS

section.heading: 1. MOS 2602, Signals Intelligence/Electronic Warfare/Cyberspace Operations

provision.text: MOS 2602, Signals Intelligence/Electronic Warfare/Cyberspace Operations Officer (III) (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DIR INTEL

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Signals Intelligence (SIGINT), Electronic Warfare (EW), Cyberspace Operations (CO) Warrant Officers supervise, direct, and provide guidance and technical expertise on all aspects of the employment of SIGINT/ EW/CO personnel, systems and facilities. These operations are in support of tactical, strategic, and national level SIGINT/EW/CO missions and include the management, collection, processing, analysis, and reporting of SIGINT and electronic warfare support (ES) derived intelligence and information, directing and supervising offensive cyberspace (OCO), planning and directing electronic attack (EA) and ES missions; and other tasks related to security and dissemination of SIGINT/EW/CO derived information. Marines in this MOS may be assigned to a BIC (within their occupational field) that has been coded with one or more DoD Cyber Workforce Framework (DCWF) work role codes. Please reference DoDI 8140.10, DoDM 8140.10, and the MOS roadmap for additional training and certification requirements associated with these work role codes.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Must successfully complete a counter-intelligence scope polygraph examination.
Must have previously served in one of the following MOSs 2611, 2621, 2629, 2631, 2641, or 2651.
Must meet eligibility and appointment criteria as prescribed in MCO 1040.42B, WO and LDO accession programs.
Must have completed the Defense Acquisition University class CLR 101, Introduction to Joint Capabilities Integration and Development System (JCIDS).
Security requirement: must have a current single scope background investigation/T5 investigation and adjudicated for sensitive compartmented information (SCI) eligibility.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements
Complete the Warrant Officer Basic Course (WOBC) (M02RMN4) within 18 months of appointment to WO.
Complete the SIGINT/EW/Cyberspace Operations Officer Course (N46B122), Marine Detachment Dam Neck, Virginia Beach, VA.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer reference (p), Signals Intelligence Training & Readiness Manual.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code. Military Officer Special and Tactical Operations Leaders/Managers, All Other 55-1019.

provision.label: f.

section.heading: 1. MOS 2712, Arabic (Modern Standard) (II/III) (Gen to 2ndLt) and (CWO5 to

provision.text: MOS 2712, Arabic (Modern Standard) (II/III) (Gen to 2ndLt) and (CWO5 to WO) EMOS, DIR INTEL

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. LinLinguist MOSs are EMOSs used in conjunction with designated billets that indicate specialized foreign language skills. Linguists supervise and participate in language translation/interpretation activities pertaining primarily to military operational and intelligence activities. The linguist MOSs will be assigned as EMOSs to identify those Marines that have attended formal language training and have achieved qualifying foreign language skills. The titles and MOSs will be used to identify billets in T/Os requiring specific foreign language skills as required by the BMOS or additional skills designator (ASD).

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites. Must be proficient in Arabic (Modern Standard).

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements

Qualifying DLPT scores alone are not justification for EMOS assignment. Marines must successfully complete the required course of instruction at the Defense Language Institute, Language Training Detachment, or designated government-funded language course and achieve minimum ILR proficiency as required by the appropriate PMOS or NMOS in two modalities of listening, reading or speaking portions of the Defense Language Proficiency Test (DLPT). (Note: By exception, individuals may qualify for this EMOS when language training is not required but Marine meets proficiency requirements and language fulfills PMOS, NMOS or billet requirements).
Maintain minimum ILR proficiency as required by the appropriate Primary MOS, Billet MOS or designated billet in two modalities of listening, reading, or speaking portions of the DLPT.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties
Conducts bi-directional consecutive interpretation of target language to English and English to target language using phraseology selected to preserve the original intent, meaning, and emphasis.
Phrases ideas to avoid language that is stilted, unnatural, and difficult to understand.
Displays an impartial attitude toward each speaker and to facts and opinions expressed.
Interprets into either English or foreign language statements made by participants in conferences, working parties, and all similar activities.
Interviews friendly non-English speaking civilians such as police, clergymen, and other Citizens to obtain information of military value.

Writes reports, including opinion as to the credibility of the person interviewed, for use by unit commander and for dissemination to lower, adjacent, and higher headquarters. 1119 NAVMC 1200.1L 1-109 Enclosure (1)
Translates into either English or the foreign language, written material of both a technical and nontechnical nature.
Establishes a file of language reference materials, English and foreign language dictionaries, and glossaries of military terms.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code. Interpreters and Translators 27-3091.

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Related Military Skill

Maintain minimum ILR proficiency as required by the appropriate primary MOS, billet MOS, or designated billet in two modalities of listening, reading, or speaking portions of the DLPT.

Interviews friendly non-English speaking civilians such as police, clergymen, and other citizens to obtain information of military value.
Writes reports, including opinion as to the credibility of the person interviewed, for use by unit commander and for dissemination to lower, adjacent, and higher headquarters.
Translates into either English or the foreign language, written material of both a technical and nontechnical nature.
Establishes a file of language reference materials, English and foreign language dictionaries, and glossaries of military terms.

section.heading: 1. MOS 2802, Electronics Maintenance Officer (Ground) (II) (LtCol to Capt)

provision.text: MOS 2802, Electronics Maintenance Officer (Ground) (II) (LtCol to Capt) PMOS, DIR C4

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Ground Electronics Maintenance Officers (2802) manage maintenance operations in the Marine forces, Marine expeditionary forces, bases, posts, and stations to include headquarters Marine Corps. They serve as the Ground Electronics Maintenance Technical Advisor on general staffs. They may command or assist in commanding a ground maintenance unit or test, evaluate, and advise in a foreign or joint environment. They provide staff level planning and technical advice concerning maintenance capabilities and supportability for ground electronics equipment to the unit, MSC, MAGTF, and MARFOR commander as well as at the enterprise level. 2802s additionally serve in a variety of billets (within their occupational field) that include the development and execution of formal training, integration of maintenance support into MAGTF operations, management of maintenance policy and doctrine, and support the requirements development and acquisition processes of ground- electronics systems and related maintenance support equipment. Marines in this MOS may be assigned to a BIC (within their occupational field) that has been coded with one or more DoD Cyber Workforce Framework (DCWF) work role codes. Please reference DoDI 8140.10, DoDM 8140.10, and the MOS roadmap for additional training and certification requirements associated with these work role codes.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Must be selected by the board to LDO.
Security requirement: secret security clearance eligibility.
This MOS may only be assigned to officers previously holding MOS 2805.
Must meet eligibility and appointment criteria as prescribed in MCO 1040.42B, WO and LDO accession programs.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements. See MOS 2805 requirements.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to reference (q), Ground Electronics Maintenance Training and Readiness Manual.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code
First-Line Supervisors/Managers of Mechanics, Installers, and Repairers 49-1011.
Managers, All Other 11-9199.

section.heading: 2. MOS 2805, Electronics Maintenance Officer (Ground) (III) (CWO5 to WO)

provision.text: MOS 2805, Electronics Maintenance Officer (Ground) (III) (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DIR C4

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Ground Electronics Maintenance Officers (2805) plan, supervise, and execute the installation, operation, and sustainment of ground electronics maintenance activities. They manage the equipment readiness, work progress, and maintenance personnel qualifications/training. They 1120 NAVMC 1200.1L 1-187 Enclosure (1) supervise the activities of personnel engaged in the recovery, salvage, and maintenance of weapon systems to include full frequency spectrum of radio systems/components, information technology networks and their subsystems, computers and handheld/mobile devices, satellite communication systems, telecommunications/video telecommunications systems, cryptographic devices, test, measurement, and diagnostic equipment, unmanned systems, artillery/fire control electronics, ground sensors; robotics, and general electronic systems/components. They supervise the eight functional areas of maintenance management, establish field maintenance sites, and supervise the security of those sites. At senior ranks, 2805’s additionally serve in a variety of billets that include the development and execution of formal training, support the requirements development and acquisition processes of ground- electronics systems and related maintenance support equipment, supervision of operational level maintenance support for ground-electronics equipment, integration of maintenance support into MAGTF operations, management of maintenance policy and doctrine, management of the training and education continuum for ground electronics maintenance personnel, and providing staff level planning and technical advice concerning maintenance capabilities and supportability for the MAGTF commander. Marines in this MOS may be assigned to a BIC (within their occupational field) that has been coded with one or more DoD Cyber Workforce Framework (DCWF) work role codes. Please reference DoDI 8140.10, DoDM 8140.10, and the MOS roadmap for additional training and certification requirements associated with these work role codes.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
This MOS may only be assigned to WOs previously qualified in MOSs 2831, 2841, 2847, 2862, 2871, 2874, or 2887.
Must meet eligibility and appointment criteria as prescribed in MCO 1040.42B, WO and LDO accession programs.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements
Complete the Warrant Officer Basic Course (WOBC) (M02RMN4) within 18 months of appointment to WO.
Complete the Electronic Maintenance Supervisors Course (EMSC/WO) (M09DNZ1), Twentynine Palms, CA.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to reference (q), Ground Electronics Maintenance Training and Readiness Manual.

section.heading: 1. MOS 3002, Ground Supply Officer (I) (LtCol to 2ndLt) PMOS, DC I&L

provision.text: MOS 3002, Ground Supply Officer (I) (LtCol to 2ndLt) PMOS, DC I&L

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Ground Supply Officers are a special staff officer that supervise the commanders' property, plant, & equipment (PP&E) and operating material & supplies (OM&S) to ensure data accuracy, existence, and completeness (equipment accountability, visibility, and auditability). They supervise and coordinate ground supply administration and operations for supply activities, units, bases, or stations, to include operating forces and shore station organizations. Ground Supply Officers may direct the activities of a maintenance distribution or industrial type organization. They command or serve in either an operating forces service unit or a non- operating forces activity. Ground Supply Officers supervise the execution of supply chain management policies and procedures pertaining to procurement, receipt, inventory control, repair, storage, distribution, issue, disposal, and computation and maintenance of stock positioning requirements. They provide supply support insight for operational planning requirements, supervise transportation of supplies and equipment, manage the transmittal of public funds, participate in the budget process, administer and expend allotted funds, and make necessary recommendations to the commanding officer regarding supply support procedures.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites. None.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements
Complete the Supply Chain Management Officer Course (M03C0G1), MCB, Camp Lejeune, NC.

Supply Officers are able to compete for MOS 3006, Operational Contract Support Officer, through the special education program (SEP) board process, which enables supply officers to attain a Master of Business Administrations degree in Acquisition and Contract Management. Officers who are not supply officers and complete the distance learning program at the Naval Post Graduate School in Contract Management Curriculum may be eligible for the 3006 additional MOS.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to reference (r), Ground Supply Training and Readiness Manual.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code
Purchasing Managers 11-3061.
Transportation, Storage, and Distribution Managers 11-3071.

provision.label: f.

section.heading: 2. MOS 3006, Operational Contract Support (OCS) Officer (I) (LtCol to Capt)

provision.text: MOS 3006, Operational Contract Support (OCS) Officer (I) (LtCol to Capt) NMOS (3002), DC I&L

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Contingency Contracting Officers (CKOs) plan, organize and accomplish contracting functions to provide supplies and services essential to Marine Corps daily operations and war-fighting mission. Included are accomplishing contracting system processes, formulating contracting policy and procedures, coordinating contracting activities and directing contracting operations. The contracting system includes effective acquisition planning, 1121 NAVMC 1200.1L 1-189 Enclosure (1) solicitation, cost, or price analysis, evaluating offers, source selection, contract award, and contract administration. In accordance with Department of Defense Operational Contract Support concepts, CKOs integrate contract support requirements into the Marine Corps operational decision-making process and into the overall unit’s spend plan. CKO’s provide contract support insight to the commander on OCS requirements and supervise the execution of policies and regulations pertaining to contract support. As a function of OCS, CKOs supervise and coordinate contract integration, contractor management and the contracting support mission. CKOs oversee the management of contract specialists, contracting officer representatives and contractor accountability within the scope of their billet. CKOs work closely with the finance and supply communities to ensure proper execution and expenditure of appropriated funds. When appointed as warranted contracting officers, in accordance with the federal acquisition regulations, CKOs have the authority to enter into, administer and terminate contracts. In this capacity, CKOs will evaluate contract requirements, specifications, bids, proposals, and subsequent contractor performance and may bind the Government only to the extent of the contracting authority granted to them.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Must possess MOS 3002.
Security requirement: secret level clearance.
Must be a captain or be selected for career designation as a first lieutenant.

Must be selected on the annual commandant's career-level education board (CCLEB) or the Naval Post Graduate School (NPS) distance learning opportunities board and complete a Master of Science in defense contract management degree.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements. Must possess a Master of Science in defense contract management degree curriculum number 815 or curriculum 835 from NPS in Monterey, CA.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to reference (r), Ground Supply Training and Readiness Manual.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code. Purchasing Managers 11-3061.

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Related Military Skill. None.

section.heading: 3. MOS 3010, Ground Supply Operations Officer (III) (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DC

provision.text: MOS 3010, Ground Supply Operations Officer (III) (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DC I&L

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Ground Supply Operations Officers are technical experts who are trained and appointed in writing to supervise and coordinate the technical activities of a supply section of the operating forces or a shore station organization. They may command or serve as a special staff officer. They advise the commander on supply related matters and provide recommended courses of action. They supervise and coordinate the technical aspects of retail (using unit and intermediate) and wholesale-level supply activities in the operating forces, supporting establishments, and with other supporting agencies. They provide the technical knowledge of automated supply systems 1121 NAVMC 1200.1L 1-190 Enclosure (1) necessary to ensure timely and accurate processing of supply related ADP systems. They provide liaison between supply sections and supporting data processing activities. They supervise supply chain management to include procurement, receipt, inventory control (i.e. forecasting/stock determination), storage, distribution, issue, disposal, and computation and maintenance of stock positioning requirements. They supervise the maintenance of subsistence, clothing, ammunition, and inventory control accounts. Ground Supply Operations Officers assist in the budget execution, fund justification, administration, and expenditure of allotted funds, and make recommendations to the commanding officer regarding supply support issues. They provide supply support insight for operational planning requirements, supervise transportation of supplies and equipment, manage the transmittal of public funds, participate in the budget process, administer, and expend allotted funds, and make necessary recommendations to the commanding officer regarding supply support procedures.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Must have previously served in MOS 3047.
Must meet eligibility and appointment criteria as prescribed in MCO 1040.42B, WO and LDO accession programs.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements
Complete the Supply Chain Management Officer Course (M03C0G1), MCB, Camp Lejeune, NC.
Complete the Intermediate Level Supply Operations Course (M03SA21), MCB, Camp Lejeune, NC.
Complete the Warrant Officer Basic Course (WOBC) (M02RMN4) within 18 months of appointment to WO.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to reference (r), Ground Supply Training and Readiness Manual.

section.heading: 1. MOS 3102, Distribution Management Officer (II/III) (LtCol to Capt) and

provision.text: MOS 3102, Distribution Management Officer (II/III) (LtCol to Capt) and (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DC I&L

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Distribution Management Officers (DMOs) are technical experts who are trained, certified, and appointed in writing to provide efficient, responsive, and quality transportation services within the assigned area of responsibility and ensure compliance with governing laws, directives, systems or programs, and regulations for cargo, passenger, personal property, and unit moves . They provide technical direction, management, and evaluation of the traffic management and unit movement aspects of the Department of Defense (DoD) transportation movement program on a worldwide basis, subject to the overall guidance, policies, and programs established by United States Transportation Command (USTRANSCOM), the Code of Federal Regulations (CFR), and DoD Components. DMOs serve throughout the MAGTF, Headquarters Marine Corps, joint organizations, COCOMs, and supporting establishments. They are responsible for multiple procurement actions, financial documentation, and payment processes for transportation services as governed within authorized policies and applicable U.S. government contracting laws. DMOs make management decisions facilitating the execution of transportation entitlements for military members, dependents, and civilian employees, and act as the contracting officer representative (COR) for various transportation service provider contracts. They provide the technical knowledge of automated information systems which deliver in-transit visibility of DoD unit and non-unit cargo, passengers, and personal property. As subject matter experts, they advise the commander on distribution and transportation related matters, provide recommended courses of action, and articulate current and future strategic distribution management requirements to the appropriate agencies. This MOS is technical in nature and requires years of training, education, and experience to become proficient.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Security requirement: secret security clearance eligibility.
Officers applying to the MOS 3102 LDO program must hold the 3102 MOS as chief warrant officers.
Must meet eligibility and appointment criteria as prescribed in MCO 1040.421B, WO and LDO accession programs.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements
Warrant Officers must complete the Warrant Officer Basic Course (WOBC) (M02RMN4) within 18 months of appointment to WO.
Complete the Distribution Management Officer Course (M0368Z1), Marine Corps Combat Service Support School, Camp Lejeune, NC.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to reference (u), Distribution Management (DMO) Training and Readiness Manual, and the Defense Transportation Regulation, Individual Missions, and Roles, and Responsibilities.

provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code. Transportation, Storage, and Distribution Managers 11-3071. 1122 NAVMC 1200.1L 1-192 Enclosure (1)

section.heading: 1. MOS 3302, Food Service Officer (II/III) (LtCol to Capt) and (CWO5 to WO)

provision.text: MOS 3302, Food Service Officer (II/III) (LtCol to Capt) and (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DC I&L

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Food Service Officers are special staff officers that supervise and manage the commanders' food service and subsistence program. They act as an interface between the commander and a wide variety of logistics agencies and organizations, while working closely with finance and supply communities to ensure the proper execution and expenditure of MPMC 1105 appropriated funds. Food Service Officers serve as technical advisers to commanders at all levels within the MAGTF, as well as supporting organizations, on the appropriate employment of food service personnel and equipment capabilities. They lead, coordinate, and integrate tailoring actions in support of the Maritime Prepositioning Force (MPF) Program, as well as the Marine Corps Prepositioning Program-Norway (MCPP-N). Food Service Officers ensure that combat feeding platforms are tailored and aligned with maritime expeditionary warfare capabilities throughout the prepositioning network. Food Service Officers plan, direct, coordinate, integrate, execute and/or supervise the execution of operations, and sustain operational forces throughout the conflict continuum for all operations, humanitarian assistance, crisis response activities, contingencies, and exercises. Food Service Officers analyze, translate, and execute commanders’ intent and operational requirements to support mission requirements across the enterprise. When forward deployed and during combat operations, or in support of humanitarian assistance/disaster relief, civil-military operations, distributed maritime operations, or other remote environments where DoD approved food sources are not established, Food Service Officers plan, direct, and coordinate actions with DoD agencies and appropriate medical authorities to ensure safe and hazardous-free food sources are obtained. When assigned to an installation command, Food Service Officers coordinate and manage installation messing and food service support, as well as perform quality control inspections of mess hall operations. They coordinate food service and messing activities at installations, units, bases, and stations, to include operating forces and shore station organizations. They provide technical assistance with the planning, budgeting, procurement, and functional layout of mess hall equipment and furniture. They shape and influence the design of dining facility construction, and rehabilitation projects for food service facilities. They administer the menu development and nutrition awareness program. This MOS is technical in nature and requires years of experience to become proficient. Due to the diversity of commands throughout the Marine Corps, some of the duties and tasks performed by the Food Service Officer may overlap with those of the supply officer and/or logistics officer. Additional billet roles may include assignment as company commander, formal school faculty, acquisition and cross-servicing arrangements (ACSA) manager, requirements development technician in coordination with the Capabilities Integration Officer at CD&I, OccFld specialist, and operations officer.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Must meet eligibility and appointment criteria as prescribed in MCO 1040.42B, WO and LDO accession programs.
Meet any additional eligibility and appointment criteria as may be prescribed in the convening MARADMIN message. 1123 NAVMC 1200.1L 1-194 Enclosure (1)
Unrestricted officers with primary MOS 3302 are preferred; however unrestricted officers with other primary MOSs may apply to the 3302 LDO program.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements

Complete the Senior Food Service Course (A14FAD1), U.S. Army Quartermaster School, Ft Gregg-Adams, VA. Any 3302 Officer who has not completed the Senior Food Service Course after two years will be considered unqualified and subject to termination.
Warrant Officers (III):

provision.label: (a)
provision.text: WOs must complete the WOBC (M02RMN4) within 18 months of appointment to WO.

provision.label: (b)
provision.text: Enlisted applicants for selection as 3302 WOs must have demonstrated food service technical qualifications through the sustained superior performance of duties within their MOS. MOS credibility is paramount to any other quality.

Limited Duty Officer Program (II): Applicants for MOS 3302 LDO shall have demonstrated technical qualifications through the superior performance of duties as an unrestricted officer. Successful tours at an installation program office, a formal learning center, as well as a deployable unit are good indicators of potential success as 3302 LDOs.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to reference (x), Food Service Training and Readiness Manual.

section.heading: 1. MOS 3402, Finance Officer (III) (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DC P&R

provision.text: MOS 3402, Finance Officer (III) (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DC P&R

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Finance Officers serve as agents of the U.S. Treasury and are responsible and pecuniary liable for the disbursement, collection, accounting, and safeguarding of all public funds entrusted to them. They are responsible for the proper execution and adherence to policies and procedures governing the valid and legal disbursement/collection of public funds. They are responsible for the maintenance of the payments generated from the master military pay account (MMPA), the computation and payment of travel entitlements, as well as other miscellaneous payments paid to or on behalf of military personnel or the Marine Corps. They are as fiscal agents responsible for the timely and accurate reporting of all expenditures and collections into the accounting system. They are advisors to the local commanders and staffs, in both a garrison and deployed environment, on all matters concerning the technical aspects of military pay and allowances, the disbursement/collection of official funds, and the laws, regulations, and directives governing their duties and other activities of the command. In garrison, they supervise and direct the operation of the finance office and are responsible for its performance. When deployed, Finance Officers supervise and direct disbursing detachments in support of the deployed commander and the Disbursing Officer. They interpret regulations and directives formulating policies and procedures relative to military pay, travel, and fiscal matters within the office and for deployed detachments. They are responsible for the formulation and adherence to adequate internal controls to govern the operations of finance offices and disbursing detachments. The appropriate command shall initiate MOS reclassification for any Marine in this MOS who receives NJP or is convicted by court-martial or civilian court for any offense involving larceny, theft, fraud, falsifying financial records, misuse of the government travel charge card (GTCC), or misuse of public funds. This MOS will be voided only by the authority of CMC.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Must have previously served in MOS 3432.
Security requirement: secret security clearance eligibility.
Must meet eligibility and appointment criteria as prescribed in MCO 1040.42B, WO and LDO accession programs.
Must have completed the Advanced Finance Course (AFC) (M03FNJ0) at the Financial Management School, Camp Lejeune, NC.
Must have no record of derogatory information or unfavorable conduct that cast doubt on the Marine’s trustworthiness and honesty.

No convictions by court-martial, civilian courts or non-judicial punishment for any disbursing related offense within the last three years to include larceny, theft, fraud, falsifying financial records, misuse of GTCC, or misuse of public funds. 1124 NAVMC 1200.1L 1-196 Enclosure (1)

section.heading: 2. MOS 3404, Financial Management Officer (I) (LtCol to 2ndLt) PMOS, DC P&R

provision.text: MOS 3404, Financial Management Officer (I) (LtCol to 2ndLt) PMOS, DC P&R

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Financial Management Officers formulate and supervise the execution of policies and procedures pertaining to the financial management of appropriated funds in the operating forces and supporting activities. The functional areas of assignment are budget formulation and execution, finance, and resource evaluation and analysis. Budget formulation and execution duties include supervising the operations of a budget office or section, providing guidance for formulation of budgets, compiling budget estimates, and reviewing and monitoring budget performance and execution. Finance duties include supervising the operations of a finance office or section within a finance office, providing guidance procedures, ascertaining the validity of disbursements and the collection of public funds, and supervising and directing the legal expenditure of public funds. Resource evaluation and analysis functions may include the evaluation and analysis of resource management issues and problems, workstation inspections, and external audits liaison.

section.heading: 3. MOS 3408, Financial Management Resource Officer (III) (CWO5 to WO) PMOS,

provision.text: Summary. Financial Management Resource Officers formulate and supervise the execution of policies and procedures pertaining to the accounting for appropriated funds supporting the operating forces and supporting establishments. Specific duties and tasks may include but are not limited to the supervision of financial management resource offices, advising commanders and comptrollers on technical aspects of accounting policy, procedures and Governmental accounting, maintaining a working knowledge of the Accounting system, identifying and reporting financial systems problems, validating accounting records for accuracy, evaluating and analyzing financial information, performing trend analysis and business process reengineering for effective and efficient use of financial resources, providing financial training to the various stakeholders, tracking accounting system changes, collaborating with interface partners, serving as a liaison with Defense Finance and Accounting Service (DFAS), serving as the financial management system expert, coordinating interfaces between business feeder systems and the accounting system, and maintaining a working knowledge of the financial reporting tools.

section.heading: 1. MOS 3510, Motor Transport Officer (III) (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DC I&L

provision.text: MOS 3510, Motor Transport Officer (III) (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DC I&L

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. The Motor Transport Officer plans, coordinates, executes and supervises the execution of all functions of motor transport. Motor Transport Officers analyze, translate, and execute commander’s operational requirements and intent to support mission requirements at the battalion, squadron, regiment, MSC, MEF and HQMC levels. As a motor transport subject matter expert, Motor Transport Officers are responsible for: planning, executing, and monitoring tactical wheeled vehicle movements, planning and forecasting of equipment readiness and availability, monitoring and managing motor transport maintenance requirements, advising commanders on motor transport maintenance and operations requirements, management of individual and collective motor transport training, and management of motor transport licensing programs. Due to the complex technical nature of motor transport, years of experience and training are required to become proficient. Depending on the unit and grade, Motor Transport Officers can be assigned as a Special Staff Officer, a Motor Transport Platoon Commander, a Motor Transport Maintenance Officer or a combination of all three.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Warrant Officers assigned to this MOS must have previously served in one of the following motor transport related MOSs 3521, 3529, 3531, or 3537.
Must meet eligibility and appointment criteria as prescribed in MCO 1040.42B, WO and LDO accession programs.

Duties consist of program, fiscal, logistical, and other managerial functions that are required to ensure oversight. Where authorized by policy, MCCS Officers also serve in direct MCCS program support billets, such as Marine Corps Exchange Supervisors and Managers. section.heading: 1. MOS 4402, Judge Advocate (I) (Col to 2ndLt) PMOS, SJA to CMC

provision.text: MOS 4402, Judge Advocate (I) (Col to 2ndLt) PMOS, SJA to CMC

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Judge Advocates provide legal support to commanders, Marines, Sailors, and their families to promote readiness and to contribute to mission accomplishment. Judge advocates provide legal support in the following six functions: military justice, international and operational law, administrative law, civil law, legal assistance, and legal administration. As company grade officers, judge advocates ordinarily serve at law centers as litigators or legal assistance attorneys, or in staff judge advocate offices as command legal advisors. Litigation opportunities exist as special trial, trial, defense, and victims legal counsel in courts-martial; as Special Assistant United States Attorneys in United States Federal Court; and as recorders, counsel for the respondent, or victims’ legal counsel in administrative discharge boards. As majors, Judge Advocates may serve as staff judge advocates or deputy staff judge advocates providing command legal advice, or as litigators in the billets of special trial counsel, military justice officer, senior defense counsel, or regional victims legal counsel. Lieutenant Colonels may serve as staff judge advocates, deputy staff judge advocates, regional special trial counsel, regional trial counsel, regional defense counsel, or Law Center Directors. Colonels may serve at Headquarters, Marine Corps, as staff judge advocates, or as the chief counsel or senior leader in the Office of Special Trial Counsel, Trial Services Organization, Defense Services Organization, or Victims Legal Counsel Organization. All field grade judge advocates may serve as military judges after being screened by a judicial screening board.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
The 4402 MOS is assigned as a primary MOS to an officer who has:

provision.label: (a)
provision.text: Obtained a juris doctor from a law school that at the time of graduation was approved by the American Bar Association (ABA).

provision.label: (b)
provision.text: Been admitted to the practice of law before a federal court or the highest court of a state, territory, commonwealth, or the District of Columbia.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements
Complete one of the following:

provision.label: (a)
provision.text: Complete the Basic Lawyer Course (N0501P1).

provision.label: (b)
provision.text: Upon the written recommendation of the SJA to CMC, the Judge Advocate General may, when in the best interests of the Marine Corps, waive the requirement to complete the Basic Lawyer Course (N0501P1), certify the officer under Article 27(b), UCMJ, and designate the officer as a judge advocate.
Any 4402 assigned to a litigation billet must complete Military Justice Orientation (N05Y221). This course may be completed immediately following completion of the Basic Lawyer Course (N0501P1).

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks refer to reference (bh), Legal Services Training and Readiness Manual. 1127 NAVMC 1200.1L 1-202 Enclosure (1)

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code

Lawyers 23-1011.

section.heading: 11. MOS 4430, Legal Administrative Officer (III) (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, SJA to

provision.text: MOS 4430, Legal Administrative Officer (III) (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, SJA to CMC

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Legal Administrative Officers are responsible for the legal administration and management functions at Law Centers, within the litigation organizations, and at those staff judge advocate offices to which they are assigned. They serve as the principal technical advisor on all legal administration and management matters, including legal information technology, fiscal and budget, and facilities. Legal Administrative Officers also serve as Law Center Directors at Law Centers geographically separated from the Regional Law Centers. As Law Center Directors, they administer and manage the day-to-day operations of the Law Center.

Must meet eligibility and appointment criteria as prescribed in MCO 1040.42B, WO and LDO accession programs.

provision.text: Requirements
Complete the Warrant Officer Basic Course (WOBC) (M02RMN4) within 18 months of appointment to WO.
Complete Judge Advocate General's Legal Center and School of the Army Warrant Officer Basic Course (A06LN41).
Judge Advocate Division, in conjunction with DC, M&RA (MMOA), is responsible for assignment of this AMOS.

provision.text: MOS 4450, Litigator (I) (Col to 1stLt) NMOS (4402), SJA to CMC

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. A Litigator is a judge advocate with the demonstrated skill and experience necessary to meet the requirements of complex and high-profile cases. Litigators contribute to the promotion of justice, the deterrence of misconduct, the facilitation of appropriate accountability, the maintenance of good order and discipline, and the promotion of efficiency and effectiveness in the military establishment. 1127 NAVMC 1200.1L 1-209 Enclosure (1)

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Must be a judge advocate.
Must be selected by a board established by the SJA to CMC.

Must possess at least 24 months of cumulative military justice experience as a trial counsel, defense counsel, victims legal counsel, appellate government or defense counsel (or corresponding billets within the Office of Military Commissions); military justice or criminal law instructor at formal schools; or military justice policy or counsel assistance program assignments at Headquarters Marine Corps or the Office of the Judge Advocate General of the Navy. Experience as a state or federal civilian prosecutor or a state or federal public defender or defense counsel, or in a litigation fellowship, may be considered on a case-by-case basis.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements. Judge Advocate Division, in conjunction with DC, M&RA (MMOA), is responsible for assignment of this AMOS.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties
May serve in any other MOS 4402 billet.
Serve in billets requiring skill and experience in military and criminal law issues, including as special trial, trial, defense, or victims legal counsel.

section.heading: 1. MOS 4502, Communication Strategy and Operations Officer (I) (LtCol to

provision.text: MOS 4502, Communication Strategy and Operations Officer (I) (LtCol to 2ndLt) PMOS, DIR COMM

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. The Communication Strategy and Operations (COMMSTRAT) officer holds the primary responsibility for communication engagement with all internal and external publics and audiences on behalf of the commander and for the execution of all plans and activities within the functions of Combat Camera (COMCAM) and Public Affairs (PA). The COMMSTRAT officer is the principal advisor to commanders and staffs on communication and visual information matters at all levels and supports all operational planning. Typical duties include, but are not limited to developing and synchronizing communication plans, monitoring and assessing the communication aspects of the information environment, to include misinformation/disinformation, identifying audiences, publics and stakeholders, identifying communication issues, risks and opportunities that may affect operations or institutional/ command reputation, conducting crisis communication, leading COMCAM and PA missions, developing annexes and appendices to operation plans, engaging with internal, domestic and international publics via traditional news media, social and/or emerging media, and face-to-face communication, to include community and key leader engagement, supervising review and release procedures, directing the development of written and visual information products, conducting communication training to assigned and supporting forces, to include media literacy and social media best practices, serving as the command printing officer, and providing support to recruiting operations.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites. Security requirement: must possess a secret security clearance and meet sensitive compartmented information (SCI) eligibility guidelines based on a single scope background investigation/T5 investigation.

provision.label: c.

section.heading: 2. MOS 4503, Visual Information Officer (III) (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DIR COMM

provision.text: MOS 4503, Visual Information Officer (III) (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DIR COMM

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. The Visual Information Officer (VIO) is a highly skilled technical expert in the 45XX occupational field, specializing in the application of organic visual information capabilities. Serving as the principal advisor to commanders and Communication Strategy and Operations (COMMSTRAT) Officers, the VIO provides expertise on all visual information matters. Their responsibilities include enhancing the proficiency and effectiveness of personnel by mentoring and training officers and Marines in mechanical, doctrinal, and conceptual aspects of visual information. VIOs play a critical role in developing training, exercises, and operational plans that support mission-essential tasks, meet communication objectives, and ensure compliance with individual and collective training and readiness standards. They manage visual information equipment and commodities within their unit, ensuring operational readiness, and they regularly report on the unit’s technical proficiency. VIOs have a comprehensive understanding of DOTMLPF-C (doctrine, organization, training, materiel, leadership and education, personnel, facilities, and cost) from a program management perspective. They are responsible for requirements management, including forecasting and analyzing financial data to support informed decisions. Additionally, VIOs oversee indoctrination and certification programs, develop annexes and appendices to operational orders, integrate emerging technologies, review training and readiness manuals, and participate in advisory groups and trade shows. They may also serve as Combat Camera (COMCAM) planners, tasked with planning, sustaining, and employing COMCAM capabilities across various operational environments. In this capacity, they work closely with numbered fleets, joint force commands (JFCs), and Headquarters Marine Corps (HQMC) to ensure the readiness of personnel and the successful execution of COMCAM operations.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Must have a GT score of 110 or higher.
Must hold PMOS 4591 with minimum of three-year experience as a 4591. 1128 NAVMC 1200.1L 1-214 Enclosure (1)
Must possess a school-trained 45XX (or legacy 43XX or 46XX) background.
Must meet eligibility and appointment criteria as prescribed in MCO 1040.42B, WO and LDO accession programs.

Security requirement: must possess secret security clearance; must meet sensitive compartmented information (SCI) eligibility guidelines based on a single scope background investigation/T5 investigation.

Must have graduated from at least one visual information management course. Eligible courses are limited to the Visual Information Management Course (A18M6N2) or the Combat Camera Leadership Course (A18A412) both at DINFOS, Ft Meade, MD.

Must have graduated from at least one visual information technical course. Eligible courses are limited to the Digital Multimedia Course (A18T4Z2), Intermediate Photojournalism Course (A1843E2), Intermediate Motion Media/Intermediate Videography Course (A18KCU2), Advanced Electronic Journalism Course (A18PNL2) all at DINFOS, Ft Meade, MD, the Department of Defense-Sponsored Military Photojournalism (MPJ) Course (C244661), or the Military Motion Media (MMM) Course (C2446P1), Military Visual Journalism Program at S.I. Newhouse School of Public Communications at Syracuse University.

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. The Career Recruiting Officer Program attracts, selects, trains, and develops career recruiting officers to be employed as principal operational advisors to command groups at all levels within the recruiting command. Career recruiting officers are chief warrant officers specifically trained in the training and employment of recruiting personnel in support of the total force recruiting mission. They assist in the development of operational plans designed to ensure mission attainment. Career recruiting officers generate reports and metrics to quantify the unit's technical and tactical proficiency for the command group. They use this information to mentor the officers and Marines of the unit in all matters required to improve the general effectiveness and proficiency of the command group and all their subordinate units. The program will be conducted in accordance with the references, focusing on mission accomplishment, career progression, and sound fiscal practices.

section.heading: 1. MOS 5502, Band Officer (II/III) (LtCol to Capt) and (CWO3 to WO) PMOS,

provision.text: MOS 5502, Band Officer (II/III) (LtCol to Capt) and (CWO3 to WO) PMOS, DIR COMM

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. MOS 5502 is assigned to Band Officers serving as either the principal or assistant director of a Marine Corps Band. They may serve as the sole Band Officer at a location, dependent on assignment, or as part of a director/assistant director leadership team. Band Officers function as special staff officers of the commanding general by providing information and recommendations on the use, current capabilities, standing procedures, and policies governing the operation of a Marine Corps Band. Band Officers serve as the officer in charge of Marine Corps Bands where they manage, administer, and coordinate musical performances, develop budgets and annual operation plans, direct internal operations and training, and supervise the employment of a Marine Corps Band. Band Officers must also maintain a working knowledge of applicable copyright regulations and directives. Band Officers regularly coordinate and liaise with their local and adjacent commands, higher headquarters, HQMC Communication Directorate, Marine Corps Recruiting Command, and other applicable agencies to provide musical support for community relations and personnel procurement programs.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Must be a graduate of the Advanced Musician Course (N0355K2) at the Naval School of Music.
Must be a graduate of the Music Unit Leader Course (N0355L2) at the Naval School of Music.
Must meet eligibility and appointment criteria as prescribed in MCO 1040.42B, WO and LDO accession programs.
Must have a recommendation letter from a band officer stating that the individual meets the minimum technical requirements.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements
Complete the Warrant Officer Basic Course (WOBC) (M02RMN4) within 18 months of appointment to WO.

In addition to eligibility criteria outlined in MCO 1040.42B, applicants must have a minimum time in service of 8 years and no more than 20 years of active naval service as of the convening date of the enlisted to WO selection board.

This MOS may only be assigned to warrant officers who were previously qualified in enlisted MOSs 5519 to 5567. Follow-on training is the Advanced Music Course (N0355K2); and the Audition Training Course (N0355N2), upon completion of the Warrant Officer Basic Course (WOBC), if not already completed.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to reference (be), Music Training and Readiness Manual.

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. MOS 5505 is assigned to those officers designated by the Secretary of the Navy to command or assist in commanding "The President's Own" U.S. Marine Band in providing music and performing such other functions as are directed by the President of the United States and the Commandant of the Marine Corps.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Must have the recommendation of the Director, U.S. Marine Band.
Security requirement: top secret security clearance eligibility (category II White House access).
Must meet eligibility and appointment criteria as prescribed in MCO 1040.42B, WO and LDO accession programs.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements. Designation by the Secretary of the Navy, pursuant to the provisions of reference (ab), Chapter 6222, Title 10, U.S. Code.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties
Serves as Commanding Officer of the U.S. Marine Band.
Serves as musical advisor to the President of the United States, the White House, and the Commandant of the Marine Corps.
Serves as principal conductor of the U.S. Marine Band and White House Chamber Orchestra and ensures professional quality musical performance, to include program selection and preparation.
Ensures direct liaison is maintained with the Commanding Officer, Marine Barracks Washington, DC regarding U.S. Marine Band administrative and logistical matters.
Ensures direct liaison is maintained with the White House for purposes of scheduling U.S. Marine Band presidential support commitments.
Ensures direct liaison is maintained with the Director, Communication Directorate, HQMC, regarding all U.S. Marine Band operational matters.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code. Music Directors and Composers 27-2041.

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Related Military Skill. None.

section.heading: 3. MOS 5506, Staff Officer, The President's Own, U.S. Marine Band (II/III)

provision.text: MOS 5506, Staff Officer, The President's Own, U.S. Marine Band (II/III) (LtCol to Capt) and (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DIR USMB

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. MOS 5506 is assigned to those officers appointed to serve as the Executive Assistant to the Director or Operations Officer of "The President's Own", United States Marine Band. These officers are permanently 1131 NAVMC 1200.1L 1-224 Enclosure (1) assigned to the U.S. Marine Band to assist the director in the performance of his nonmusical duties and responsibilities.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Must have a recommendation of the Director, U.S. Marine Band.
Security requirement: top secret security clearance eligibility (category II White House access).
Must meet eligibility and appointment criteria as prescribed in MCO 1040.42B, WO and LDO accession programs.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements. None.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties
Executive Assistant to the Director (II):

provision.label: (a)
provision.text: Serves as chief administrator of the U.S. Marine Band and as primary counsel to the director on Marine Corps matters.

provision.label: (b)
provision.text: Coordinates and supervises the operation, maintenance and inventory of all U.S. Marine Band support staff sections.

provision.label: (c)
provision.text: Maintains direct liaison with the Commanding Officer, Marine Barracks Washington, DC, and appropriate staff agencies at HQMC regarding non-musical matters of the U.S. Marine Band.

provision.label: (d)
provision.text: Functions as the U.S. Marine Band Supply, Fiscal and Training Officer.
Operations Officer (III):

provision.label: (a)
provision.text: Maintains direct liaison with the White House for purposes of scheduling all U.S. Marine Band presidential support commitments and requisite rehearsals.

provision.label: (b)
provision.text: Maintains direct liaison with the Director, Communication Directorate, HQMC, for the purpose of scheduling all U.S. Marine Band official commitments and requisite rehearsals not involving presidential support.

provision.label: (c)
provision.text: Advises the Director on U.S. Marine Band operational matters.

provision.label: (d)
provision.text: Directs the activities of the U.S. Marine Band operations office and stage crew.

provision.label: (e)
provision.text: Manages the recruiting program for MOS 5511.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code. Music Directors and Composers 27-2041.

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Related Military Skill. None. 1131 NAVMC 1200.1L 1-225 Enclosure (1)

section.heading: 4. MOS 5507, U.S. Marine Drum and Bugle Corps Officer (II/III) (LtCol to 1st

provision.text: MOS 5507, U.S. Marine Drum and Bugle Corps Officer (II/III) (LtCol to 1st Lt) and (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DIR USMB

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. A Drum and Bugle Corps Officer manages, administers, and coordinates the musical performance, internal operations, training, and employment of "The Commandant's Own," The U.S. Marine Drum and Bugle Corps (D & B Corps). As Commanding Officer, Executive Officer, or Operations Officer of the D & B Corps Company, , will discharge applicable company level duties and act as technical advisor to the Commanding Officer of Marine Barracks on all matters pertaining to the utilization of the Drum and Bugle Corps.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites. Must meet eligibility and appointment criteria as prescribed in MCO 1040.42B, WO and LDO accession programs.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements
Complete the Warrant Officer Basic Course (WOBC) (M02RMN4) within 18 months of appointment to WO.
Must have served as a member of the "The Commandant's Own," The United States Marine Drum and Bugle Corps.
Must complete an audition/interview administered by the commanding officer, the U.S. Marine Drum and Bugle Corps and other designated senior personnel as directed by the commanding officer.
Recommendations will be forwarded to CMC, via the Commanding Officer, Marine Barracks, Washington, DC for review and consideration.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to reference (be), Music Training and Readiness Manual.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code. Music Directors and Composers 27-2041.

provision.label: f.

section.heading: 1. MOS 5702, Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear (CBRN) Defense

provision.text: MOS 5702, Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear (CBRN) Defense Officer (III) (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DC PP&O

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Chemical, Biological, Radiological, And Nuclear Defense (CBRND) Officers are technical advisers for operational and tactical functions associated with CBRN protection, CBRN response, and CBRN support to countering weapons of mass destruction (CWMD). They support an organization’s planning process by providing CBRN subject matter expertise for plans, annexes, orders, and standard operating procedures. CBRND Officers serving in protection billets develop plans to support their commander’s schemes of maneuver under CBRN conditions. CBRND Officers serving in response billets plan and lead CBRND support to the MAGTF and joint forces. CBRND Officers serving in CBRN analysis billets apply subject matter expertise to information and intelligence to develop a threat picture to guide the commanders planning and decision-making cycles. CBRND Officers in senior-level management billets (MEU, MEF, MARFOR) develop plans and advise commanders and staffs on requirements related to activates and requirements to support combatant commander’s CWMD lines of effort and objectives within the supported area of operations. Marines entering this OccFld will initially receive a basic MOS 5701, Basic Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear Defense Officer. Depending on the level of command, CBRND Officers will fill billets as CBRND/CWMD Plans Officer, CBRND Officers, CBRN Protection Officers, or CBRN Response Officers.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Must meet eligibility and appointment criteria as prescribed in MCO 1040.42_, warrant officer (WO) and limited duty officer (LDO) accession programs.
Applicants considered for selection as a warrant officer in MOS 5702 must be the rank of sergeant or above.
Security requirement:

provision.label: (a)
provision.text: Active secret clearance. This is required prior to attendance of the CBRN Defense Basic Warrant Officer Course (BWOC), USMC CBRN Defense School, Ft Leonard Wood, MO.

provision.label: (b)
provision.text: For CWO4/CWO5: must meet sensitive compartmented information (SCI) eligibility guidelines based on a single scope background investigation (SSBI)/Tier 5 (T5) investigation. This is required in performance of duties associated with MARFOR to MSC and joint billet(s).

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements
Complete the Warrant Officer Basic Course (WOBC) (M02RMN4), The Basic School, Quantico, VA within 18 months of appointment to WO.

Complete the CBRN Basic Warrant Officer Course (A16EGI4), at U.S. Marine Corps CBRN School, Ft Leonard Wood, MO. Officers will normally complete the CBRN course immediately upon graduation from WOBC to qualify for and be awarded MOS 5702. Any 5701 officer who has not completed the CBRN 1132 NAVMC 1200.1L 1-227 Enclosure (1) Basic Warrant Officer Course after two years will be considered unqualified and subject to termination.
Additional skill progression and skill enhancement courses see MOS 5702 MOS road map.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks refer to reference (ap), Chemical, Biological, and Nuclear (CBRN) Defense Training and Readiness Manual.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code
Mid-level Management Marines (CWO3 to WO1) holding mid-level management ranks perform the related duties from the entry level ranks with the following additional classifications:

provision.text: First-Line Supervisors/Managers of Officer and Administrative Support Workers 43-1011.

provision.label: (b)

provision.label: (c)
provision.text: Emergency Management Specialists 13-1061.
Senior-Level Management Marines (CWO5 to CWO4) holding senior level management ranks perform the related duties from the previous classifications with the following classifications:

provision.label: (a)
provision.text: Command and Control Center Specialists 55-3015.

provision.label: (b)
provision.text: General and Operations Managers 11-1021.

provision.label: (c)
provision.text: Management Analyst 13/14-1111.
