Advisor, 0570.
Operational Advisor, 0571. 1133 NAVMC 1200.1L 1-228 Enclosure (1) 1133. OCCUPATIONAL FIELD 58, MILITARY POLICE, INVESTIGATIONS, AND CORRECTIONS

section.heading: 1. MOS 5803, Military Police Officer (I) (LtCol to 2ndLt) PMOS, DC I&L

provision.text: MOS 5803, Military Police Officer (I) (LtCol to 2ndLt) PMOS, DC I&L

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Military Police Officers perform garrison law enforcement duties at supporting establishments (SE) and operating forces (OPFOR) law enforcement duties within Marine Forces Headquarters and within 4th Law Enforcement Battalion, Marine Forces Reserve. Typical duties and billets at the SE include watch commander, services officer, operations officer, deputy provost marshal, and provost marshal. Typical duties and billets at the OPFOR include platoon commander, company commander, operations officer, executive officer, and commanding officer, and law enforcement integrations officer.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Must qualify for and graduate The Basic School.

Must have no history of mental, nervous, or emotional disorders. Waivers will not be considered for those Marines determined unsuitable for assignment as a Military Police Officer by a medical professional.

Must have no convictions by special or general courts-martial or felony convictions or misdemeanor convictions of domestic violence from civil courts. Waivers will not be granted for convictions by special or general courts-martial or civil courts for crimes of domestic violence as per reference (bk), the Lautenberg Amendment.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements. Complete the Military Police Officers Basic Course (A1670Z3), at MARCORDET, Ft Leonard Wood, MO.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to reference (ac), Military Police and Corrections Training and Readiness Manual for OccFld 58.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code. First-Line Supervisors/Managers of Police and Detectives 33-1012.

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Related Military Skill. None.

section.heading: 2. MOS 5804, Corrections Officer (III) (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DC I&L

provision.text: MOS 5804, Corrections Officer (III) (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DC I&L

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Corrections Officers interpret, apply and review policies, regulations and directives, oversee the humane care, custody, discipline, safety, welfare, and correctional treatment of personnel confined at military correctional facilities (MCFs), review and recommend treatment programs, custody classification and other security, control and disposition matters related to the confinement or restraint of personnel. They review and make recommendations on clemency, parole and/or restoration to duty requests and other day-to-day requests from confined and restrained personnel. They investigate disturbances and recommend actions regarding discipline and adjustment, research and prepare correspondence and reports. They direct the operational, administrative and logistical activities of a brig regarding personnel administration, supply, training activities, messing, pay and funds accounts, and discipline. Corrections Officers also direct counseling and rehabilitation programs. Corrections Officers also provide commanders with 1133 NAVMC 1200.1L 1-229 Enclosure (1) the mission and immediate oversight of regional detention facilities in theater with subject matter expertise on the safe, humane and efficient care of enemy detainees entrusted to their care. Duties and billets include Administration Officer, Programs Officer, Operations Officer, Marine Corps Absentee Collection Center OIC, Detachments OIC, Revocation Hearing Officer, Brig Officer, Executive Officer, and Commanding Officer.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Must currently hold PMOS 5831.
Must meet eligibility and appointment criteria as prescribed in MCO 1040.42B, WO and LDO accession programs.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements. Complete the Warrant Officer Basic Course (WOBC) (M02RMN4) within 18 months of appointment to WO.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to reference (ac), Military Police, Investigation, and Corrections Training and Readiness (T&R) Manual for OccFld 58.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code. First-Line Supervisors/Managers of Correctional Officers 33-1011.

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Related Military Skill
Correction and Detention Specialist, 5831.
Correctional Counselor, 5832.

section.heading: 3. MOS 5805, Criminal Investigation Officer (III) (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DC PP&O

provision.text: MOS 5805, Criminal Investigation Officer (III) (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DC PP&O

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Criminal Investigation Officers function as the officer in charge of the Criminal Investigation Division (CID), operationally assigned to either a Provost Marshal’s Office (PMO)/Marine Corps Police Department or a deployed/combat unit. Criminal Investigation Officers manage and provide subject matter expertise on criminal investigative operations in both supporting establishment and deployed/ combat contingency environments. Criminal Investigation Officers also liaise and coordinate with local, state, and federal law enforcement agencies on behalf of the provost marshal.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Must have clarity of speech.
Must have normal color vision (may not be waived).
Security requirement: top secret with SCI eligibility.
Must have a valid state driver's license (may not be waived).
Must have previously attended the U.S. Army Criminal Investigation Division Special Agent Course (CIDSAC) (A1601D3) and been awarded MOS 5821.

Must have a minimum height of 59 inches. In pursuit of safety, waivers to the height requirements in reference (at), standard licensing policy for operating military vehicles will not be granted. 1133 NAVMC 1200.1L 1-230 Enclosure (1)

No convictions by summary special or general court martial or civil courts (except minor traffic violations); non-judicial punishment convictions involving illegal drugs, spouse abuse/domestic violence, or immoral character (may not be waived).

Must have no history of mental, nervous, or emotional disorders. If previous treatment has been received the health care practitioner will be contacted to determine if the Marine under consideration has a condition that could impair judgment, reliability, or the ability to perform the duties of a Criminal Investigations Officer. Waivers will not be considered for those Marines determined unsuitable for assignment as a Criminal Investigator by a medical professional.

In addition to the above requirements, Reserve Marines must be currently employed with a recognized civilian law enforcement agency as a sworn peace officer, currently holding the billet of a criminal investigator with a minimum of three years investigative experience may be awarded the 5805 MOS by successfully completing the CID OJT program with favorable endorsement from the overseeing CID Officer and receive an eligibility letter from the head, Criminal Investigation Division, CMC PS.

All above prerequisites must be met a to be selected as a 5805 CID Investigations Officer within the reserve component a Marine must also currently possess the PMOS 5821 and have successfully completed CID Special Agent Course (7H-F73/832-31D20/30), U.S. Army Military Police Schools (USAMPS), Ft Leonard Wood, MO or the USAMPS distance education course identification number CID Special Agent-832-31D20/30(RC) (DL) (P).

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements. Complete the Warrant Officer Basic Course (WOBC) (M02RMN4) within 18 months of appointment to WO.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to reference (ac), Military Police, Investigation, and Corrections, Training and Readiness Manual for OccFld 58.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code. First-Line Supervisors/Managers of Police and Detectives 33-1012.

section.heading: 1. MOS 5902, Electronics Maintenance Officer Aviation Command and Control

provision.text: MOS 5902, Electronics Maintenance Officer Aviation Command and Control (C2) (II) (LtCol to Capt) PMOS, DC AVN

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. The Electronics Maintenance Officer Aviation Command and Control (C2) Officers supervise and coordinate the installation, operation, and maintenance of all aviation C2 electronic systems and equipment used by the Marine Air Command and Control Systems (MACCS) units, Littoral Anti-Air Battalion (LAAB), and Air Traffic Control (ATC) systems at Marine Corps Air Stations (MCAS). Lead communications planner for the MACCS in expeditionary amphibious base operations for ensured C2 during littoral operations in a contested environment. Fleet marine forces billet assignments for this officer will be in the S-6 at the squadron or group level within the marine air control group, battalion S-6 at the LAAB and Low Altitude Air Defense (LAAD). Non-Fleet marine forces billet assignments for the Electronics Maintenance Aviation C2 Officers include billets at the Marine Corps Communication-Electronics School, Marine Aviation Training Support Group 23, Training and Education Command, Marine Corps Tactical Systems Support Activity, Acquisition Project Officer at Marine Corps Systems Command, Requirements Officer at Marine Corps Combat Development Command, and occupational field manager at Headquarters Marine Corps.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Security requirement: top secret or top secret with sensitive compartmented information eligibility.
Must meet eligibility and appointment criteria as prescribed in MCO 1040.42B, WO and LDO accession programs.

This MOS may only be assigned to officers previously qualified in one of the following MOSs 5910, Aviation Radar Maintenance Officer, 5950, Air Traffic Control System Maintenance Officer, or 5970, Tactical Data Systems Maintenance Officer.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements

This MOS is career progression for officers in MOSs 5910, 5950, and 5970. MOS is assigned after Marine is promoted to captain. All 5902s are highly encouraged to attend the following courses based on their current duty assignments and previous career training:

provision.label: (a)
provision.text: JT-101 Introduction to Joint Multi-TDL Network (MTN) Operations (J30 P-US1380).

provision.label: (b)
provision.text: Weapons and Tactics Instructor Course (M149731).

provision.label: (c)
provision.text: Link 16 Joint Interoperability Course (J3O P-US109).

provision.label: (d)
provision.text: Marine Air Traffic Control Maintenance Managers Course (N23KCN2).

provision.label: (e)
provision.text: Multi-Tactical Data Link Advanced Joint Interoperability Course (A05L6Z1 or A05L6ZM). 1134 NAVMC 1200.1L 1-232 Enclosure (1)

provision.label: (f)
provision.text: Defense Acquisition University ACQ 1010 Fundamentals of Systems Acquisition Management via DAU at https://icatalog.dau.edu.

provision.label: (g)
provision.text: Defense Acquisition University ACQ 1010 Fundamentals of Systems Acquisition Management via DAU at https://icatalog.dau.edu.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties
Collects and analyzes maintenance data to permit system/equipment performance evaluation.
Provides information concerning the capabilities, limitations, and reliability of ground electronic systems and equipment.
Reviews estimates and justifications for funds required for the maintenance of aviation command and control electronic systems and equipment.

Manages the status of equipment, progress of work, parts availability, training, qualifications of maintenance personnel, and advises the commanding officer on all technical matters pertaining to ground electronic systems and equipment.

Supervises and coordinates the activities of sections engaged in the installation, operation, and maintenance of ground electronic systems and equipment used in the Marine Air Command and Control System and Marine Corps Air Stations.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code
Mangers, All Others 11-9199.
First-Line Supervisors/Managers of Mechanics, Installers, and Repairers 49-1011.

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Related Military Skill
Aviation Radar Systems Officer, 5910.
Air Traffic Control Systems Officer, 5950.
Tactical Data Systems Officer, 5970.

section.heading: 2. MOS 5910, Aviation Radar Systems Officer (III) (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DC AVN

provision.text: MOS 5910, Aviation Radar Systems Officer (III) (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DC AVN

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Aviation Radar Systems Officers are specifically trained in the site selection, installation, operation, maintenance, and repair of the surveillance and fire control radar systems within the marine air command and control system (MACCS). Aviation Radar Systems Officers supervise and coordinate all task and maintenance related actions completed by the aviation radar technicians in the radar maintenance section. They assist the commander in coordination and future planning in support of operations and exercises. The Aviation Radar Systems Officer coordinates the execution of current operations and provides garrison support to operations in support of resident and deployed detachments. Fleet marine forces billet assignments for this officer will be in the marine air control group and littoral anti- air battalion. Non-Fleet marine forces billet assignments for the Aviation Radar Systems Officer include training and maintenance officer at the Marine 1134 NAVMC 1200.1L 1-233 Enclosure (1) Corps Communication-Electronics School, Maintenance Officer at the Marine Corps Logistics Base, Maintenance Officer at the Marine Corps Tactical Systems Support Activity, Acquisition Project Officer at Marine Corps Systems Command, and Requirements Officer at Marine Corps Combat Development Command. The Aviation Radar Systems Officer should complete the MACCS Warrant Officer’s Course after selection to WO. PMOS is not dependent upon the completion of this course. Upon appointment to warrant officer, PMOS 5910 is assigned.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Security requirement: secret security clearance eligibility.
This MOS may only be assigned to warrant officers who were previously qualified in enlisted MOS 5948 or 5953.
Must meet eligibility and appointment criteria as prescribed in MCO 1040.42B, warrant officer and limited duty officer accession programs.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements
MOS is assigned after the Marine is promoted to warrant officer.
Complete the MACCS Warrant Officer Course (M0968K1) Twentynine Palms, CA.
Complete the Warrant Officer Basic Course (WOBC) (M02RMN4) within 18 months of appointment to WO.

This is a highly technical MOS and requires that the Aviation Radar Systems Officer be educated and thoroughly knowledgeable in electronics theory, propagation effects, radar waveform theory, radar system elements, advanced radar techniques, and differing radar systems and applications.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties
Provide advanced technical analysis during the planning, installation, operation, and maintenance of the aviation radar systems.
Responsible for all radar systems, support equipment, and electronics maintenance personnel assigned to the radar section.
Supervises the highly complex repairs or modifications to the air surveillance and fire control radar systems.
Assigned responsibility for one or more of the air defense surveillance radar systems and associated equipment.
Informs the commanding officer and Communications-Electronics Officer on the progress of work and status of the radar equipment.
Ensure records are accurately maintained and maintenance performed conforms to established standards and is recorded in GCSS-MC.
Coordinate with higher level commands, activities, and depots on all maintenance related activities and life cycle management of the aviation radar systems. 1134 NAVMC 1200.1L 1-234 Enclosure (1)
Maintains a thorough familiarity with both surveillance and fire control radar systems and their associated MARK XIIA Identification Friend or Foe subsystems.
Ensure that maintenance personnel maintain the tools, repair parts, test equipment, facilities, and publications needed to perform the level of maintenance authorized.
Ensures that assigned aviation radar technicians are adequately trained and that all radar equipment is maintained in an operational condition capable of supporting the command's mission.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code
Mangers, All Others 11-9199.
First-Line Supervisors/Managers of Mechanics, Installers, and Repairers 49-1011.

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Related Military Skill
Aviation Radar Technician, 5948.
Air Traffic Control Radar Technician, 5953.

section.heading: 3. MOS 5950, Air Traffic Control Systems Officer (III) (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DC

provision.text: MOS 5950, Air Traffic Control Systems Officer (III) (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DC AVN

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Air Traffic Control (ATC) Systems Officers supervise and coordinate the installation, sighting, operation, training, maintenance, and repair of ATC and meteorology and oceanography (METOC) systems and equipment. Must possess a detailed, working knowledge of all Navy sponsored aviation maintenance programs and processes governed by the Naval Aviation Maintenance Program Manual and familiarization with the ground equipment maintenance program. Fleet marine forces billet assignments for this officer will be in the marine air control group. Non-Fleet Marine Forces billet assignments for this officer include maintenance billets at marine corps air stations, marine corps air facilities, and marine corps installation command. The ATC Systems Officer should complete the Marine Air Traffic Control Maintenance Management Course and Joint Aviation Supply and Maintenance Material Management Course after selection to warrant officer. PMOS is not dependent upon the completion of these courses. Upon appointment to warrant officer, PMOS 5950 is assigned.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Security requirement: secret security clearance eligibility.
Must meet eligibility and appointment criteria as prescribed in MCO 1040.42B, WO and LDO accession programs.
This MOS may only be assigned to warrant officers who previously were qualified in the enlisted MOSs 5951, 5952, 5953, or 5954.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements
Complete the Marine Air Traffic Control Maintenance Mangers Course (N23KCN2). 1134 NAVMC 1200.1L 1-235 Enclosure (1)
Complete the Warrant Officer Basic Course (WOBC) (M02RMN4) within 18 months of appointment to WO.
MOS is assigned after Marine is promoted to warrant officer.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties
Supervises operation and maintenance of specific ATC and METOC systems and common ground equipment used in Marine ATC companies or in Marine ATC facilities.

Manages the status of equipment, progress of work, repair parts requirements, training and qualification of maintenance personnel, and advises on all technical matters pertaining to the ATC and METOC systems and equipment.
Provides information concerning capabilities, limitations, and reliability of ATC and METOC systems and equipment.
Communications planner for ATC services in expeditionary amphibious base operations and ensures command and control for littoral operations in a contested environment.
Collects and disseminates technical instructions and directives applicable to the maintenance and operation of systems and equipment.
Prepares timely estimates and justification for funds required for the maintenance of installed systems and equipment.
Maintains authorized allowances of tools and test and support equipment.
Administers the preventive and corrective maintenance program.
Conducts maintenance management of assigned equipment.
Collects and analyzes maintenance data for reports.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code
Mangers, All Others 11-9199.
First-Line Supervisors/Managers of Mechanics, Installers, and Repairers 49-1011.

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Related Military Skill
Aviation Meteorological Equipment Technician, 5951.
Air Traffic Control Navigational Aids Technician, 5952.
Air Traffic Control Radar Technician, 5953.
Air Traffic Control Communications Technician, 5954. 1134 NAVMC 1200.1L 1-236 Enclosure (1)

section.heading: 4. MOS 5970, Tactical Data Systems Officer (III) (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DC AVN

provision.text: MOS 5970, Tactical Data Systems Officer (III) (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DC AVN

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Tactical Data Systems (TDS) Officers supervise and coordinate the siting, installation, operation, training, maintenance, and repair of aviation command and control (AC2) tactical data systems (TDS), and the Marine Air Defense Integrated System (MADIS) within the Marine Air Command and Control System (MACCS). The TDS Officer provides the commander with expert technical advice regarding the employment, security, installation, and performance of ground based air defense (GBAD) and AC2 TDS infrastructure within service, joint, coalition, and garrison environments. Must possess a detailed working knowledge of all voice, tactical data communications, and GBAD systems found within the Marine Air Control Group and within the Marine Littoral Regiments. Fleet Marine Forces billet assignments for this officer will be in the Marine Air Control Group and the Marine Littoral Regiment. Non-Fleet Marine Forces billet assignments for the Tactical Data Systems Officer include Training and Maintenance Officer at the Marine Corps Communication-Electronics School, TDS Maintenance Officer at the Marine Corps Tactical Systems Support Activity, and Acquisition Project Officer at Marine Corps Systems Command. The Tactical Data Systems Officer should complete the MACCS Warrant Officer course after selection to warrant officer. PMOS is not dependent upon the completion of this course. Upon appointment to warrant officer, PMOS 5970 is assigned.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Security requirement: secret security clearance eligibility.
This MOS may only be assigned to Warrant Officers who were previously qualified in enlisted MOSs 5939, 5974, or 5979.
Must meet eligibility and appointment criteria as prescribed in MCO 1040.42B, WO and LDO accession programs.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements
Complete the MACCS Warrant Officer Course (M0968K1).
MOS is assigned after the Marine is promoted to warrant officer.
Complete the Warrant Officer Basic Course (WOBC) (M02RMN4) within 18 months of appointment to WO.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties

Provide advanced technical analysis during the planning, installation, operation, maintenance and secure integration of TDS network architectures, tactical data link systems, radio communication systems, end- user computers, servers, and system software/firmware.
Assist in the development of training and employment plans designed to ensure mission essential task compliance.
Supervise diagnosis, field level repairs, and modifications to communications and data systems.

Supervises and coordinates the activities of electronic maintenance personnel engaged in the siting, installation, operations, maintenance, and repair of AC2 TDS within the MACCS. 1134 NAVMC 1200.1L 1-237 Enclosure (1)
Informs the Commanding Officer as to the status of equipment, progress of work, and advises on matters pertaining to this equipment.
Supervises the keeping of maintenance records and collects data for reports.
Supervises the reporting of failures and the requisitioning, receipt, and allocation of tools, parts, and materials.
Instructs personnel in the mission, function, use, and procedures for operating AC2 TDS.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code
First-Line Supervisors/Managers of Mechanics, Installers, and Repairers 4-1011.
Mangers, All Others 11-9199.

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Related Military Skill
Aviation Communication Systems Technician, 5939.
Tactical Data Systems Technician, 5974.
Tactical Air Operations/Air defense Systems Technician, 5979.

section.heading: 5. MOS 5977, Weapons and Tactics Instructor Aviation Command & Control (AC2)

provision.text: MOS 5977, Weapons and Tactics Instructor Aviation Command & Control (AC2) Maintenance Officer (II/III) (LtCol to Capt) and (CWO5 to CWO2) NMOS (5902, 5910, 5950, 5970), DC AVN

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Weapons and Tactics Instructor AC2 Maintenance Officers train and evaluate Marine air command and control personnel on aviation sensors and weapons systems in the employment of the Marine Air Command and Control System (MACCS) to support the Marine Air Ground Task Force.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites. Must hold MOS 5902, 5910, 5950, or 5970.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements. Must successfully complete the MAWTS-1 Weapons and Tactics Instructor Course (M149731).

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties
Manage a unit's Weapons and Tactics Training Program.

Perform classroom and operational instruction on various facets of MACCS equipment/weapons systems including integration, employment capabilities and limitations in support of the MAGTF and joint tasking.
Analyze performance and provide corrective guidance.
Instructs on current enemy capabilities and tactics to counter their threat.
Recommend the most qualified personnel for nomination to the Weapons and Tactics Instructor Course and unit instructor qualifications. 1134 NAVMC 1200.1L 1-238 Enclosure (1)
Ensures all training adheres to established training standards, safety, and ORM procedures.

provision.label: e.

provision.label: f.

section.heading: 1. MOS 6002, Aircraft Maintenance Officer (I) (LtCol to 2ndLt) PMOS, DC AVN

provision.text: MOS 6002, Aircraft Maintenance Officer (I) (LtCol to 2ndLt) PMOS, DC AVN

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Aircraft Maintenance Officers (AMOs) supervise and coordinate aircraft maintenance and repair activities. To be effective, 6002 AMOs must possess a detailed, working knowledge of all Navy-sponsored aviation maintenance programs and processes governed by CNAFINST 4790.2 series. MOS 6002 AMOs are different from MOS 6004, Aircraft Maintenance Engineer Officers in that they are unrestricted officers whose career paths can lead to the command of a Marine Aviation Logistics Squadron (MALS) or to designation as an Acquisition Professional.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites. None.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements
Lateral moving, unrestricted officers:

provision.label: (a)
provision.text: Be recommended by their command for assignment of MOS 6002.

provision.label: (b)
provision.text: Perform at least 12 months of on-the-job training in an aircraft maintenance billet.

provision.label: (c)
provision.text: Complete the Joint Aviation Supply and Maintenance Material Management Course (N0530O3).

provision.label: (d)
provision.text: Complete the Naval Aviation Maintenance Program Management Course (N42P2M2) at NAS Pensacola, FL.
Unrestricted entry-level officers must complete the Naval Aviation Maintenance Program Indoctrination Course (N42FDA2) at Whiting Field, FL.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties
Organizes and supervises the maintenance and repair of aircraft, aircraft components, and aviation support equipment.
Supervises the scheduling of aircraft for inspection.
Informs commanding officers of work progress and advises them on matters pertaining to aircraft maintenance.
Ensures the material condition and mission capability of the weapon systems and the collection and dissemination of maintenance management information.
Directs technical training and establishes safety programs for maintenance personnel.
Establishes maintenance procedures and assigns personnel to key billets.
Directs and monitors requisitioning, receipt, and allocations of materials and tools. 1135 NAVMC 1200.1L 1-240 Enclosure (1)

Pursue Defense Acquisition Workforce Improvement (DAWIA) Certification in order to gain qualifications prior to entering senior billets within the MOS (see MOSs 8057 or 8058). The three primary areas of study typically applicable to AVLOG are:

provision.label: (a)
provision.text: Life Cycle Logistics (LCL).

provision.label: (b)
provision.text: Program, Quality, Manufacturing (PQM).

provision.label: (c)
provision.text: Program Management (PM).

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code. First-Line Supervisors/Managers of Mechanics, Installers, and Repairers 49- 1011.

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Related Military Skill. None.

section.heading: 2. MOS 6004, Aircraft Maintenance Engineer Officer (II/III) (LtCol to Capt)

provision.text: MOS 6004, Aircraft Maintenance Engineer Officer (II/III) (LtCol to Capt) and (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DC AVN

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Aircraft Maintenance Engineer Officers (AMEOs) are responsible for management of aircraft maintenance and aeronautical repair matters. To be effective, AMEOs must possess a detailed, working knowledge of all Navy sponsored aviation maintenance programs and processes governed by reference (af). AMEOs must possess skills in managing resources with emphasis on efficient personnel employment, maintaining equipment readiness, and exercise/deployment planning. A high level of technical expertise is required to manage the execution of tasks within aviation maintenance. A small population of AMEO's are placed throughout Marine Corps aviation, complementing the talents of the MOS 6002 population. Unlike the 6002, whose career path and school may lead to command, the 6004 will remain focused on the technical, procedural, planning and managerial details associated with organizational and intermediate level maintenance in support of shore based, sea based, and expeditionary operations. Warrant Officers and junior chief warrant officers generally serve in flying squadrons while more senior chief warrant officers generally serve as division officers within the Marine Aviation Logistic Squadron (MALS). While the minimum requirements in paragraph (b) serve as a threshold, a range of characteristics indicating management knowledge exist including training and documented management knowledge/skill. Management experience in organizational and intermediate levels both provide solid backgrounds for this restricted officer MOS as the task of an AMEO is to plan and solve complex management problems and not to have specific knowledge of repairing any one equipment or aircraft type. Applicants with both organizational and intermediate level maintenance experience are considered ideal candidates for appointment to MOS 6004 limited duty officer (LDO). MOS 6004 shall not be assigned as a secondary MOS.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Must meet eligibility and appointment criteria as prescribed in MCO 1040.42B, WO and LDO accession programs.

Limited Duty Officer Program: officers applying to the MOS 6004 LDO program must hold the 6004 MOS as chief warrant officers and achieve selection by the board to LDO. 1135 NAVMC 1200.1L 1-241 Enclosure (1)

Must hold a feeder MOS of 60XX, 61XX, 62XX, 63XX, 64XX, or 65XX. Applicants shall hold an additional MOS of 6011, 6012, or 6018 and have served successfully in maintenance control, production control, or quality assurance for a minimum of 18 months. MOS 6004 LDO applicants must possess the 6004 MOS.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements
Complete the Naval Aviation Maintenance Program Management Course (N42P2M2) Milton, FL.
Warrant Officers must complete the Warrant Officer Basic Course (WOBC) (M02RMN4) within 18 months of appointment to WO.

Warrant Officers (III): enlisted Marines applying for selection as 6004 warrant officers must meet the prerequisites in paragraph 2.b. and have demonstrated aviation maintenance technical qualifications through sustained superior performance of duties within their MOS. Demonstrated and sustained management skill within a feeder MOS supervisory billet such as work center supervisor and quality assurance or maintenance controller is paramount to any other quality.
Limited Duty Officers (II):

provision.label: (a)
provision.text: Only 6004 warrant officers may apply for appointment as 6004 LDOs.

provision.label: (b)
provision.text: Applicants for MOS 6004 LDO must have demonstrated aviation maintenance technical qualifications through the superior performance of duties as 6004 Warrant Officers. A successful tour within maintenance control in a flying squadron is a primary indicator for future success as a 6004 LDO.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties. For a detailed listing of duties refer to reference (ad) COMNAVFORINST 4790.2 and (bn) NAVMC 4790.1.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code. First-Line Supervisors/Managers of Mechanics, Installers, and Repairers 49- 1011.

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Related Military Skill. None.

section.heading: 3. MOS 6044, Additive Manufacturing Officer (II) (Maj to 2ndLt) NMOS (0402,

provision.text: MOS 6044, Additive Manufacturing Officer (II) (Maj to 2ndLt) NMOS (0402, 6002, 6004, 6302, 6502, 6602, 6604), DC AVN

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Additive Manufacturing Officers provide additive manufacturing capability to the Marine Aviation Logistics Squadron (MALS) units by operating computer aided design software and various types of 3D printing machines. This MOS will be assigned as a NMOS.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites. Must be designated as one of the following PMOSs 0402, 6002, 6004, 6302, 6502, 6602, or 6604.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements
Complete the T&R level 1000 qualification. 1135 NAVMC 1200.1L 1-242 Enclosure (1)
Must be associated with and actively maintaining the T&R qualification requirements to perform AM duties for work center 550 over a period of at least 9 months.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties
The duties and tasks will be as prescribed and designated in references:

provision.label: (a)
provision.text: Reference 4790.1, Aviation Maintenance and Supply Training and Readiness Program.

provision.label: (b)
provision.text: Reference 4790.2, Naval Aviation Maintenance Program.

provision.label: (c)
provision.text: Reference MCO P4790.1, Maintenance Training and Management Evaluation Program.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code
Commercial and Industrial Designers 27-1021 design and develop manufactured products.
Computer Occupations, Other 15-1299 computer aided design.

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Related Military Skill. None.

section.heading: 4. MOS 6077, Weapons and Tactics Instructor (II/III) (LtCol to 2ndLt) and

provision.text: MOS 6077, Weapons and Tactics Instructor (II/III) (LtCol to 2ndLt) and (CWO5 to WO) NMOS (6002, 6004, 6302), DC AVN

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Weapons and Tactics Instructors train aviation maintenance professionals in the execution of various tasks that are encompassed within a wide spectrum of aviation maintenance and logistics matters. They will (1) Assist their respective unit commanders in conducting a professional Marine Corps Aviation Weapons and Tactics Training Program (WTTP) which includes specific individual MOS training and collective operational unit training;

Act as aviation logistics managers and planners with enhanced planning skills and insight into integrating all aviation assets to promote mission success; (3) Coordinate and conduct appropriate supplementary courses applicable to their particular community; (4) Ensure all training conducted under their supervision is properly documented and adheres to established safety procedures; (5) Submit appropriate information, including exercise/ deployment reports, to assist MAWTS-1 in updating tactics and instruction.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites. Must possess Primary MOSs 6002, 6004, or 6302.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements. Complete the Marine Aviation Weapons and Tactics Squadron One Advanced Aircraft Maintenance Officer Course (M14FDG1).

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties

Serves as the aviation logistics and maintenance management standardization representative to the organizational and intermediate level units on all issues relating to training standards, training development, training management, and evaluation.
Provides training and readiness (T&R) guidance and serves as the official signature authority for T&R signoffs within their assigned scope. 1135 NAVMC 1200.1L 1-243 Enclosure (1)
Reviews, investigates, introduces, and evaluates emerging standardization techniques and ensures the broadest dissemination to the fleet.
Coordinates and facilitates professional development opportunities and classroom training for maintenance professionals ensuring standardization IAW the most current fleet practices.
Serves as a maintenance operations planning liaison providing expertise to units planning large scale detachments and deployments.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code. Teachers and Instructors, All Other, Except Substitute Teachers, 25-3097.

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Related Military Skill. None. 1136 NAVMC 1200.1L 1-244 Enclosure (1) 1136. OCCUPATIONAL FIELD 63, ORGANIZATIONAL AVIONICS MAINTENANCE

section.heading: 1. MOS 6302, Avionics Officer (II/III) (LtCol to Capt) and (CWO5 to WO)

provision.text: MOS 6302, Avionics Officer (II/III) (LtCol to Capt) and (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DC AVN

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Avionics Officers (AVOs) direct the Avionics division/ department efforts in order to provide leadership, coordination, and technical subject matter expertise in support of the organizational/ intermediate level mission. Cognizant areas of oversight include aircraft maintenance, avionics systems and component maintenance, avionics support equipment maintenance, integrated logistics resource management, and technical professional development. AVOs are the subject matter experts on all avionics related matters and serve as the staff advisor to the commanding officer and other staff officers throughout the organization. The AVO is directly responsible to the commanding officer for the management, administration, and control of the Electronic Countermeasures (ECM), Aircraft Survivability Equipment (ASE), on-aircraft Digital Interoperability (DI) systems and the (Local Element) Key Management Infrastructure (KMI) System program. Warrant Officers and junior Chief Warrant Officers (CWO2/3) generally serve in operational flying squadrons while more senior Chief Warrant Officers (CWO4/5) generally serve as Assistant AVOs within the Marine Aviation Logistic Squadron (MALS) or AVOs at training commands. Additionally, unique billets (i.e. fleet introduction team, HMX-1, VMX-1) will expose AVOs to program management, acquisitions, and manpower production/management experiences. Management experience in both the organizational and intermediate levels provide solid backgrounds for the restricted officer 6302 MOS as the task of an AVO is to plan and solve complex management problems and not to have specific knowledge of repairing any one equipment or aircraft type. Applicants with a wide breadth of aircraft platforms and avionics systems, program management, and acquisitions expertise are considered ideal candidates for appointment to MOS 6302 limited duty officer (LDO). MOS 6302 shall not be assigned as a secondary MOS.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Security Requirement: secret security clearance eligibility.
This MOS shall only be assigned to personnel with a primary MOS of either 63XX or 64XX.
Must meet eligibility and appointment criteria as prescribed in MCO 1040.42B, WO and LDO accession programs.

Proficiency and expertise are typically identified by collateral duty inspector, collateral duty quality assurance representative, and quality assurance representative designations (AMOS 6016, 6017, or 6018). Any of these designations are indicators of a Marines technical expertise within an assigned MOS. Applicants may also be considered if they possess an additional designation as a production controller or maintenance controller (AMOS 6011/ 6012).

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements
Limited Duty Officers (II):

provision.label: (a)
provision.text: Only 6302 chief warrant officers shall apply for appointment as 6302 LDOs. 1136 NAVMC 1200.1L 1-245 Enclosure (1)

provision.label: (b)
provision.text: Applicants for MOS 6302 LDO must have demonstrated superior avionics expertise through the exemplary performance of duties as a 6302 chief warrant officer. A successful tour in a flying squadron is a primary indicator for future success as a 6302 LDO.
Warrant Officers (III):

provision.label: (a)
provision.text: Newly promoted 6302 warrant officers must complete The Basic School Warrant Officer Basic Course (WOBC) (M02RMN4), Quantico, VA within 18 months of appointment to WO.

provision.label: (b)
provision.text: Warrant Officers must complete the first available Avionics Officer/Avionics Chief Foundation Course (N2362X2) at NAS Pensacola, FL.

provision.label: (c)
provision.text: Specific assigned billets, coded with an additional skill designator (ASD), must attain the appropriate type and level certification through the Defense Acquisition University (DAU) within 24 months (see MOS 8060). The three primary areas of study typically applicable to AVLOG are:

provision.label: (d)
provision.text: Life cycle logistics.

provision.label: (e)
provision.text: Program management.

provision.label: (f)
provision.text: Production, quality, manufacturing.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties

Responsible to the commanding officer for the operation of the avionics division/department, to include operational, technical, and administrative functions, asset utilization, and configuration management of all squadron avionics assets.

Advise the maintenance officer on all avionics division/ department matters pertaining to the ability to support squadron maintenance efforts, training requirements, personnel qualifications, calibration requirements, and current and planned projects within the avionics division/ department.

Directs and monitors all avionics logistical transactions, negotiating avionics maintenance evolutions based on supply availability and aviation maintenance demands while evaluating the effectiveness of avionics to respond to published flying hour programs.

Ensures all avionics personnel are trained, certified, and capable of safely repairing aircraft, aeronautical components, and aviation support equipment within the scope of their MOS in accordance with applicable instructions.
Responsible for the proper handling, updating, managing, auditing, and safeguarding of classified avionics aircraft publications and equipment.

Manages and maintains mission essential kits that effect: Communication, Navigation, Instrumentation (CNI) Mission Systems, on-aircraft Digital Interoperability (DI) Mission Systems, Aircraft Survivability Equipment (ASE), Targeting Systems, and Fire Control Systems including all Controlled Cryptographic Item (CCI) and related COMSEC management to ensure assigned squadrons have required capabilities as directed by higher. 1136 NAVMC 1200.1L 1-246 Enclosure (1)

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code. First-Line Supervisors/Managers of Mechanics, Installers, and Repairers 49- 1011.

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Related Military Skill. None. 1137 NAVMC 1200.1L 1-247 Enclosure (1) 1137. OCCUPATIONAL FIELD 65, AVIATION ORDNANCE

section.heading: 1. MOS 6502, Aviation Ordnance Officer (II/III) (LtCol to Capt) and (CWO5 to

provision.text: MOS 6502, Aviation Ordnance Officer (II/III) (LtCol to Capt) and (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DC AVN

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. The Aviation Ordnance Officer manages all aviation ordnance logistics, maintenance, and operations functions, as well as all aircraft weapon systems and Aircraft Armament Systems (AAS).

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
LDOs must also achieve selection by the board to LDO.
Must have previously served in one of the following MOSs 6531, 6541, or 6591.
Must meet eligibility and appointment criteria as prescribed in MCO 1040.42B, WO and LDO accession programs.
Security requirement: secret security clearance eligibility (some key billets require top secret security clearance eligibility).

WOs/CWOs must have successfully completed the Aviation Ordnance AO "A" Enlisted Course (N23G3U2) and must have demonstrated aviation ordnance qualification and expertise through substantially documented performance of associated duties and tasks.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements
Warrant Officers must complete the Warrant Officer Basic Course (WOBC) (M02RMN4) within 18 months of appointment to WO.
Warrant Officers must successfully complete the Aviation Ordnance Managers Career Progression Level I (AOMCP) Course (N42G3N3), NAS Whiting Field, FL.
CWO3s and LDO Captains should complete the Aviation Ordnance Managers Career Progression Level II (AOMCP) Course (N42G4N3), NAS Whiting Field, FL.
CWO4s, CWO5s, LDO majors, and LtCols should complete the Aviation Ordnance Managers Career Progression Level III Course (N42G4M3), NAS Whiting Field, FL.
Marines serving in billets coded with an additional skill designator (ASD) as per the table of organization must attain the appropriate skill within 24 months of billet assignment.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties

Direct and supervise all personnel engaged in the storage, handling, transportation, inventory, maintenance, issue, and repair of aviation munitions, AAS, and Armament Weapons Support Equipment (AWSE).

Manage the assignment and execution of all work task codes authorized via the personnel qualification/certification program for Class V ammunition and explosives. 1137 NAVMC 1200.1L 1-248 Enclosure (1)
Evaluate aviation ordnance policies, processes and procedures for accuracy, thoroughness, efficiency, and compliance with higher policy/ doctrine and promulgate changes when necessary.
Direct and supervise the aircraft armament system program, ensuring all equipment adheres to associated documentation, repair and provisioning processes and standards.
Direct the command explosives safety program and serve as the command explosives safety officer.
Manage the command Class V(A) inventory accuracy and inventory management programs.
Administer the explosive handler’s qualification and certification program and serve as the certification board chairperson.
Promulgate and publish command aviation ordnance standard operating procedures and ensure timely submission of all required aviation ordnance reports.
Supervise the allocation, requisitioning, positioning, receipt, status and the ammunition transaction reporting of the command's aviation munitions.

Pursue defense acquisition workforce improvement (DAWIA) certification in order to gain qualifications prior to entering senior billets within the MOS (see MOS 8060). The two primary areas of study typically applicable to AVLOG are:

provision.label: (a)
provision.text: Life cycle logistics (LCL).

provision.label: (b)
provision.text: Program management (PM).

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code. None.

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Related Military Skill. None.

section.heading: 2. MOS 6577, Aviation Ordnance Weapons and Tactics Instructor (II/III)

provision.text: MOS 6577, Aviation Ordnance Weapons and Tactics Instructor (II/III) (LtCol to Capt) and (CWO5 to WO) NMOS (6502), DC AVN

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Ordnance Officer, qualification/certification board chairperson or staff billet are subject matter experts (SME) on the tactical employment of expeditionary aviation ordnance operations. AO WTI Marine Officers support MAGTF and squadron commanders by maintaining safety and operational standards, readiness levels and possess the knowledge required to successfully plan, brief, and execute any technique, tactic or procedure authorized in our warfighting doctrine. They are intimately familiar with all aspects of leading an ordnance division/department in any expeditionary environment or operation. They are experts in forward arming refueling points/forward operational bases/ distributed aircraft operations and expeditionary advanced based operation concepts.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites. Must hold a 6502 MOS.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements. Must successfully complete the MAWTS-1 Expeditionary Ordnance Course (MEOC) (M14G221). 1137 NAVMC 1200.1L 1-249 Enclosure (1)

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties. As an Expeditionary Ordnance Subject Matter Expert, they must be able to effectively and accurately articulate current and future capabilities of a unit’s ordnance division/department based on current structure, manpower and qualifications. Identify potential problems and solve all issues related to logistical considerations, requirements and capabilities, execution, potential contingencies and retrograde of all weapons and personnel while observing and adhering to all orders and regulations regarding explosive safety. Increase the squadron commander’s capability and lethality by creating, providing and briefing innovative solutions and improvements to plans, minimizing risk and increasing combat effectiveness. Responsible for providing the most capable and highest trained ordnance division/department to commanders IOT accomplish any given task.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code. Teachers and Instructors, All Other 25-3099.

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Related Military Skill. None. 1138 NAVMC 1200.1L 1-250 Enclosure (1) 1138. OCCUPATIONAL FIELD 66, AVIATION LOGISTICS

section.heading: 1. MOS 6602, Aviation Supply Officer (I) (LtCol to 2ndLt) PMOS, DC AVN

provision.text: MOS 6602, Aviation Supply Officer (I) (LtCol to 2ndLt) PMOS, DC AVN

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Aviation Supply Officers are unrestricted officers who may command or assist in commanding a Marine aviation logistics squadron. Aviation Supply Officers may also achieve designation as an acquisition professional. Aviation Supply Officers are responsible for planning, directing, and controlling the performance and execution of aviation supply functions within Marine aircraft wings, Marine aviation logistics squadrons, Marine Corps air stations, naval expeditionary vessels, and various TYCOM and SYSCOM staffs. This requires in-depth familiarity and working knowledge sufficient to supervise and control Navy-developed and sponsored aviation logistics information management systems, repairable material management programs, financial management programs, budgeting and accounting functions, aviation inventory management functions, and warehousing operations. Aviation Supply Officers must ensure that aviation supply operations sustain the unit's combat readiness and enhance its ability to perform its mission. They must be able to establish division and department goals and to develop and execute plans to achieve those goals. They must monitor supply management indicators to assist in tracking performance over time and ensure progress towards accomplishment of established goals. Aviation Supply Officers must initiate and maintain liaison with external agencies to provide or obtain support and to report supply management indicators. They must also initiate and maintain liaison with maintenance personnel in the operational squadrons and the intermediate maintenance department so that they have a clear appreciation of the needs of their customers.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites. Security requirement: secret security clearance eligibility.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements
Complete the Marine Aviation Supply Officer Basic Qualification Course (N42C0B3), Milton, FL.

Marines serving in billets coded with an additional skill designator (ASD) as per the table of organization must attain the appropriate certification level through the Defense Acquisition University (DAU) within 24 months of billet assignment.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties
For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to reference (ae), Aviation Logistics Individual Training Standards.

Pursue Defense Acquisition Workforce Improvement (DAWIA) Certification in order to gain qualifications prior to entering senior billets within the MOS (see MOS 8060). The three primary areas of study typically applicable to AVLOG are:

provision.label: (a)
provision.text: Life Cycle Logistics (LCL).

provision.label: (b)
provision.text: Production, Quality, Manufacturing (PQM).

provision.label: (c)
provision.text: Program Management (PM). 1138 NAVMC 1200.1L 1-251 Enclosure (1)

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code. Transportation, Storage, and Distribution Managers 11-3071.

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Related Military Skill. None.

section.heading: 2. MOS 6604, Aviation Supply Operations Officer (III) (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DC

provision.text: MOS 6604, Aviation Supply Operations Officer (III) (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DC AVN

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Aviation Supply Operations Officers are responsible for the performance of aviation supply activities within Marine Aviation Logistics Squadrons, Marine Aircraft Wings, Marine Corps Air Stations, and naval expeditionary vessels. A high level of expertise is required to supervise the execution of the various tasks encompassed within the wide spectrum of aviation supply support. To be effective, Aviation Supply Operations Officers must possess detailed and working knowledge of all Navy-developed and sponsored aviation logistics information management systems, repairable management programs, financial management programs, budgeting and accounting functions, aviation inventory management systems and functions, and warehousing operations. They must be skilled in working with a variety of ashore and afloat automated systems such as relational supply (R-Supply), the Naval Aviation Logistics Command Management Information Systems (NALCOMIS), F-35 Autonomic Logistics Information System (ALIS), Supply Chain Management (SCM), and other. They must be able to effectively use information extracted from these systems to aid in supervision and control. In addition, Aviation Supply Operations Officers must have detailed knowledge of all applicable Navy Supply documents, forms, and publications and must be proficient in working with Navy Supply afloat procedures, to include the support of deployed aviation operations. Aviation Supply Operations Officers must ensure that aviation supply operations support and sustain the unit's combat readiness and enhance the unit's ability to perform its mission. They must establish and maintain liaison with external agencies while providing or obtaining support and reporting supply management indicators. A working knowledge in acquisitions, life cycle logistics, and program management is highly desirable for senior 6604 billets.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Security requirement: secret security clearance eligibility.
This MOS may only be assigned to Warrant Officers who were previously qualified in MOS 6672.
Must meet eligibility and appointment criteria as prescribed in MCO 1040.42B, WO and LDO accession programs.

provision.text: Requirements
Complete the Marine Aviation Supply Officer Basic Qualification Course (N42C0B3), Milton, FL.
Complete the Warrant Officer Basic Course (WOBC) (M02RMN4) within 18 months of appointment to WO.

Marines serving in billets coded with an additional skill designator (ASD), as per the table of organization, must attain the appropriate certification level through DAU within 24 months of billet assignment. 1138 NAVMC 1200.1L 1-252 Enclosure (1)

provision.text: Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to reference (bn), Aviation Maintenance and Supply Training and Readiness Program (AMSTRP).

section.heading: 3. MOS 6607, Aviation Logistician (II/III) (LtCol to 2ndLt) and (CWO5 to WO)

provision.text: MOS 6607, Aviation Logistician (II/III) (LtCol to 2ndLt) and (CWO5 to WO) NMOS (6002, 6302, 6502, 6602), DC AVN

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Aviation Logisticians are assigned to selected headquarters and staffs. They are trained in aviation logistics (AVLOG) support plan development. The skill set provides headquarters staffs with aviation logistics specific subject matter expertise to support the force deployment planning and execution process, exercise planning, pre-positioning program development execution, and doctrine development.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Security requirement: secret security clearance eligibility.

Must possess PMOSs 6002, Aircraft Maintenance Officer, MOS 6004, Aircraft Maintenance Engineer Officer, MOS 6302, Avionics Officer, MOS 6502, Aviation Ordnance Officer, MOS 6602, Aviation Supply Officer, or MOS 6604, Aviation Supply Operations Officer.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements
Complete at least two of the following courses:

provision.label: (a)
provision.text: Joint Logistics Course (JLC) (A14L232) at the U.S. Army Logistics University (ALU), Ft Gregg-Adams, VA.

provision.label: (b)
provision.text: Joint Operations Planning and Execution System (JOPES) Action Officer Course (JAOC) (JD2101) at Ft Eustis, VA.

provision.label: (c)
provision.text: Joint Operations Planning and Execution System (JOPES) Support Personnel Course (JSPC) (JD1102) at Ft Eustis, VA. 1138 NAVMC 1200.1L 1-253 Enclosure (1)

provision.label: (d)
provision.text: Maritime Prepositioning Force (MPF) Staff Planning Course, covered by the Expeditionary Warfare Training Group (CIN: K-2E-3119) or (N03L8Q1 or N30L8Q1).

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties
Serve as AVLOG representative for operational planning teams and crisis action teams.
Support the development, review, and update of OPLANS/CONPLANS in support of higher headquarters' directives.
Review/validate time phased force deployment data to ensure compliance with guidance and directives.
Develop estimates of supportability and concepts of logistics support.
Support the development and operational orders and letters of instruction for ACE operations and exercises.

Administrative Services Managers 11-3011.
Transportation, Storage, and Distribution Managers 11-3071.
Logisticians 13-1081.
Operations Research Analysts 15-2031.

provision.text: Related Military Skill. None.

section.heading: 4. MOS 6608, AIRSpeed Officer (II/III) (LtCol to 2ndLt) and (CWO5 to WO)

provision.text: MOS 6608, AIRSpeed Officer (II/III) (LtCol to 2ndLt) and (CWO5 to WO) NMOS (6XXX), DC AVN

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. AIRSpeed Officers are assigned to selected headquarters and staffs. They are trained to institute a culture of self-sustaining, continuous process improvement aligned toward delivering increased readiness at reduced resource cost. AIRSpeed Officers are responsible to provide the planning, training, integration, sustainment, and monitoring of best business practices (Theory of Constraints (TOC), LEAN, and Six Sigma within aviation logistics.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Must be trained in Jonah.
Must be trained and certified as supply chain design expert (SCDE).
Must be trained and certified as supply chain technical expert (SCTE).
Must possess MOS 6XXX: aviation maintenance, avionics, aviation ordnance, or aviation supply MOS. 1138 NAVMC 1200.1L 1-254 Enclosure (1)

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements. Must complete AIRSpeed Black Belt Job Qualification Requirement (JQR) as defined by COMNAVAIRFOR, or equivalent course as approved by HQMC Aviation (ASL).

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties
Coordinate, support, and monitor TOC process designs and deployments.
Coach LEAN events, including Rapid Improvement Events (RIEs), Value Stream Analyses (VSAs), and 5S events.
Act as team leader for complex LEAN Six Sigma (LSS) events or projects where statistical analysis is required.
Ensure all AIRSpeed department core members are Green Belt qualified, at a minimum.
Be responsible for administering and evaluating AIRSpeed events. Function as liaison with external consultants and/or organizations.
Ensure sustainment of improvement through use of follow-ups and refresher training.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code. Logisticians 13-1081.

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Related Military Skill. None.

section.heading: 5. MOS 6609, Aviation Logistics Information Systems Advisor (LtCol to 2ndLt)

provision.text: MOS 6609, Aviation Logistics Information Systems Advisor (LtCol to 2ndLt) and (CWO5 to WO) NMOS (0602, 6002, 6004, 6602, 6604), DC AVN

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Aviation Logistics Information Systems Advisors are assigned to selected headquarters and staffs. They possess knowledge of how to establish, employ, and sustain Aviation specific information systems in support of Marine Corps and Naval Aviation and are able to communicate clearly with a non-technical audience. Their role is to integrate and coordinate with the plans sections or operations sections of their respective command as it pertains to Aviation Information Systems. They must identify and clearly translate communications and Department of Defense Information Network Operations (DODIN Ops) capabilities, limitations, and opportunities in all phases of the planning cycle. The skill set provides headquarters staffs with officers who, along with MOS 6694 subject matter expertise, ensure that aviation information systems are considered in the force deployment planning and execution process, exercise planning, pre-positioning program development execution, and doctrine development.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Security requirement: secret security clearance eligibility.

Must possess one of the following PMOSs MOS 6002, Aircraft Maintenance Officer, MOS 6004, Aircraft Maintenance Engineer Officer, MOS 6602, Aviation Supply Officer, MOS 6604, Aviation Supply Operations Officer, or MOS 0602, Communications Officer.

provision.text: Requirements. Must have minimum of 6 months of time in a table of organization designated 6609 MOS billet. 1138 NAVMC 1200.1L 1-255 Enclosure (1)

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties
Identify and clearly translate aviation information systems capabilities, limitations, and opportunities in all phases of the planning cycle.
Support the development, review, and update of OPLANS/CONPLANS in support of higher headquarters' directives.
Develop estimates of supportability and concepts of logistics support.
Support the development and operational orders and letters of instruction for ACE operations and exercises.

section.heading: 1. MOS 6802, Meteorological and Oceanographic (METOC) Services Officer (II/

provision.text: MOS 6802, Meteorological and Oceanographic (METOC) Services Officer (II/ III) (LtCol to Capt) and (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DC I

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Meteorological and Oceanographic (METOC) Service Officers plan, direct, and lead METOC operations at all levels of the operating forces and the supporting establishment. They are subject matter experts on all aspects of the METOC discipline and the application of it within the decision-making process. Operating force billet assignments operating force billet assignments for this officer include marine expeditionary forces, marine air wings, intelligence battalions, littoral anti-air battalions, marine littoral regiment, and marine air traffic control companies within the marine air control squadrons. Non-operating forces billet assignments for this officer include deputy commandant for information, HQMC, director of intelligence, deputy commandant for aviation, aviation enablers, chief of naval operations, N2N6E, naval information warfare center pacific, marine corps air stations, marine corps detachment Keesler AFB, marine aviation weapons & tactics squadron one, and marine corps intelligence schools. METOC Officers require excellent verbal and written communication skills, advanced competency in meteorology and littoral oceanography, and comprehension of geospatial intelligence (GEOINT) concepts.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Must meet eligibility and appointment criteria as prescribed in MCO 1040.42B, WO and LDO accession programs.
Security requirement: must meet sensitive compartmented information (SCI) eligibility guidelines based on a single scope background investigation/T5 investigation.
Marines applying for selection as 6802 warrant officer must have MOS 6842, the journeyman METOC analyst forecaster designation and successfully served five or more years in a 6842 billet.

LDO Program: officers applying to the MOS 6802 LDO program must hold the 6802 MOS as CWOs, have the NMOS 6877, have a journeyman METOC officer (JMO) designation, and achieve selection by the board to LDO.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements
METOC warrant officers are required to complete the following courses:

provision.label: (a)
provision.text: Complete the Warrant Officer Basic Course (WOBC) (M02RMN4) within 18 months of appointment.

provision.label: (b)
provision.text: Complete the METOC Officer Course (N469752), Marine Corps Intelligence Schools, Dam Neck, VA after graduation from WOBC. Any 6802 who has not completed the METOC Officer Course within two years of appointment will be considered unqualified and subject to termination. METOC Officers who were commissioned prior to 2022 are exempt from this requirement. 1139 NAVMC 1200.1L 1-257 Enclosure (1)
METOC chief warrant officers are required to complete the following courses and to be eligible for selection to LDO captain:

provision.label: (a)
provision.text: Joint METOC Officers Course (JS-DDGO).

provision.label: (b)
provision.text: Weapons and Tactics Instructor Course (M14P2A1).

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties. For a complete list of duties and tasks, refer to MCRP 2- 10B.6, MAGTF Meteorological and Oceanographic Operations and NAVMC 3500.38, Meteorological and Oceanographic Training and Readiness Manual.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code. Atmospheric and Space Scientists 19-2021.

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Related Military Skill. None.

section.heading: 2. MOS 6877, Weapons and Tactics Instructor (WTI) METOC (II/III) (LtCol to

provision.text: MOS 6877, Weapons and Tactics Instructor (WTI) METOC (II/III) (LtCol to Capt) and (CWO5 to WO) NMOS (6802), DC I

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Weapons and Tactics Instructors-Meteorological and Oceanographic (METOC) Services Officers train personnel on environmental characterization and effects in relation to aviation operations in support of the MAGTF and aviation ground equipment, sensor, and weapon system performance in relation to enemy threats. WTI-METOC Officers are proficient in the development of environmental sensing plans to characterize the physical environment and operational orders development required for designated staff billets. This MOS is assigned only as an NMOS to qualified METOC Officers and qualifies Chief Warrant Officers for the LDO program.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Must hold MOS 6802.
Must hold the senior instructor (SI) designation per the MAWTS-1 Command, Control, and Communication (C3) Course Catalog.
Security requirement: must have a current single scope background investigation/T5 investigation and adjudicated for sensitive compartmented information (SCI) eligibility.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements. Must successfully complete the MAWTS-1 Weapons and Tactics Instructor Course (M149721) Yuma, AZ.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties
Management of local or subordinate METOC technical training programs.
Identify technical training shortfalls that prevent or hinder the development of METOC products in support of decision makers.
Develop or assist in the development of technical training that improves METOC support to decision makers.
Identify new or emerging METOC doctrinal support methods through Marine Corps Lessons Learned. 1139 NAVMC 1200.1L 1-258 Enclosure (1)
Develop or assist in the development of new METOC Tactics, Techniques & Procedures (TTPs) from Marine Corps Lessons Learned.
Develop the Annex H of a MAGTF or MSC operational order or plan to support Marine Corps, Joint, or Coalition operations in support of contingencies.
Develop MAGTF environmental collection plans that integrate with Joint Coalition environmental sensing strategies to support Marine Corps operations in support of contingencies.
Identify METOC sensitivities for MAGTF systems and operations to establish METOC thresholds to support all elements of the MAGTF by understanding the impact of the physical environment.
Identify METOC sensitivities for enemy systems and operations to establish METOC thresholds to determine opportunities for exploitation of the physical environment by friendly forces.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code. Teachers and Instructors, All Other 25-3099.

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Related Military Skill. None. 1140 NAVMC 1200.1L 1-259 Enclosure (1) 1140. OCCUPATIONAL FIELD 70, AIRFIELD SERVICES

section.heading: 1. MOS 7002, Expeditionary Airfield and Emergency Services Officer (III)

provision.text: MOS 7002, Expeditionary Airfield and Emergency Services Officer (III) (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DC AVN

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. The Expeditionary Airfield and Emergency Services Officer conducts planning for and oversees the installation, operation, and maintenance of airfield surfacing materials, expeditionary visual landing aids, and aircraft recovery equipment. In addition, these officers conduct the planning for and direct structural and aircraft firefighting, rescue, and salvage and recovery operations.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
This MOS may only be assigned to warrant officers who previously were qualified in one of the following enlisted MOSs 7011 and 7051.

Must meet the medical standards as required per reference (bc), The National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) 1582 and reference (cq), The Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) 29 Code of Federal Regulation (CFR) 1910.234.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements
Complete the Warrant Officer Basic Course (WOBC) (M02RMN4) within 18 months of appointment to WO.
WO:

provision.label: (a)
provision.text: Complete the Marine Expeditionary Airfield Advance Course (N2370L2) at NAS, Pensacola, FL.

provision.label: (b)
provision.text: Complete the Marine Expeditionary Airfield Equipment Course (N2370D2) at NAS, Pensacola, FL.

provision.label: (c)
provision.text: Complete the Fire Protection Apprentice (Air Force) Course (F0764T2) at Goodfellow Air Force Base, San Angelo, TX.

provision.label: (d)
provision.text: Complete the Marine Survey and Assault Zone Assessment (MSAAZA) Course at MAWTS-1 Yuma, AZ.
CWO2 to CWO5:

provision.label: (a)
provision.text: Complete the MAWTS-1, Weapons and Tactics Instructors Course (M149731) at MAWTS-1 Yuma, AZ.

provision.label: (b)
provision.text: Complete the Contingency Airfield Pavement Evaluation (CAPE) Course, Air Force Civil Engineer Support Agency Tyndall, Air Force Base, FL.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to reference (dp), Marine Expeditionary Airfield/Emergency Services Officers (EAESO) Training and Readiness Manual.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code. Airfield Operations Specialists 53-2022.

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Related Military Skill. None. 1140 NAVMC 1200.1L 1-260 Enclosure (1)

section.heading: 2. MOS 7077, Weapons and Tactics Instructor-Aviation Ground Support (II/III)

provision.text: MOS 7077, Weapons and Tactics Instructor-Aviation Ground Support (II/III) (LtCol to 1stLt) and (CWO5 to WO) NMOS (0402, 1302, 7002), DC AVN

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Aviation Ground Support-Weapons and Tactics Instructors function as advisors to the commander and coordinate all Marine Air/Ground Task Force (MAGTF) Aviation Ground Support (AGS) requirements. Operating forces billet assignments for this NMOS include Marine aircraft wing, marine wing support group, marine wing support squadron, and marine wing support detachment. Non-operating forces billet assignments for this NMOS include HQMC AXE-10, Marine aviation and weapons tactics squadron one, Marine Corps air station, and tactical training exercise control group. The AGS WTI’s educational requirements include planning and executing of airfield and air base construction/repair and services, airfield security operations, airfield damage repair, base recovery after attack, forward arming and refueling point operations, and aircraft salvage/recovery. Additionally, both officers and staff noncommissioned officers with this NMOS can be used to plan, train, and assess AGS for the Marine aircraft wing.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
MOSs 1310, 1390, or 7002 must be a CWO.
MOSs 0402 or 1302 must be LtCol to 1stLt.
Must have 12 months operating force experience.
Must be or have served in a MAW, MAG, MWSS, or MWSD.
Security requirement: secret security clearance eligibility.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements. Must successfully complete the MAWTS-1 Weapons and Tactics Instructor Course (M149731) Yuma, AZ.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties
Manages a unit's weapons and tactics training program.
Plans and executes the Unit Readiness Program.
Analyzes performance and provides corrective guidance.
Instructs on current enemy capabilities and tactics to counter their threat.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code. Teachers and Instructors, All Other 25-3099.

section.heading: 1. MOS 7202, Command and Control Officer (I) (LtCol to Maj) PMOS, DC AVN

provision.text: MOS 7202, Command and Control Officer (I) (LtCol to Maj) PMOS, DC AVN

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Air Command and Control Officers plan and coordinate the activities of Marine Air Command and Control Systems (MACCS) agencies. They advise commanders on matters pertaining to integration and joint employment of the MACCS. Air Command and Control Officers are relied upon to execute the decentralized control of assigned aircraft and missiles in the MAGTF Area of Operations (AO). Air Command and Control Officers plan, organize, direct, and manage tactical operations. These include tactical control of aircraft and air traffic control, surface and airborne fires integration, unmanned aircraft integration, radar network management, tactical data link operations, airspace planning and the employment of ground based air defense (GBAD). They command or assist in commanding such units. The Joint Air Operations Center Air Command and Control Course (JAOC2C) (F19L2W2), JT-101 Introduction to Multi-Tactical Data Link Network Operations Course (JT- 101Intro to MTN OPS), JT-102 Multi-TDL Advanced Joint Interoperability Course (JT-102 MAJIC) (A05L6Z1), JT-201 Multi-TDL Network Planners Course (A05KHY1), JT-301 Joint Interface Control Officers Course (JT-301 JICO) (A05FH21), Military Airspace Management Course (F0273D1), MAWTS-1 Air Command and Control Officers Course (ACCOC) (M1467Q1), MAWTS-1 ACE Battle-Staff Officer Course (ABOC), MAWTS-1 TACC University Course, MAWTS-1 Senior Watch Officer (SWO) Course, and the MAWTS-1 Weapons and Tactics Instructor (WTI) Course (M149731) are available as skills enhancement training for the Air Command and Control Officer.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Must have normal color perception.
Hearing loss no greater than 15db between 500-2,000 Hz.
Must have 20/20 vision (may be correctable to 20/20 with eyeglasses or contact lenses).
Security requirement: top secret with sensitive compartmented information access eligibility.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements. Unrestricted Officers holding a primary MOS from OccFld 72 will be assigned MOS 7202 upon promotion to the grade of major.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to 72XX Aviation Training and Readiness (T&R) Manual.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code. Command and control Center Officers 55-1015.
