section.heading: 10. MOS 0491, Logistics/Mobility Chief (MGySgt to GySgt) PMOS, DC I&L

provision.text: MOS 0491, Logistics/Mobility Chief (MGySgt to GySgt) PMOS, DC I&L

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. The Logistics/Mobility Chief coordinates, plans, conducts, and supervises logistics operations throughout various levels of the Marine 3111 NAVMC 1200.1L 3-53 Enclosure (1) Corps. They serve on general officer staffs at the MEF, MARFOR, and HQMC level where they conduct planning and execution of MAGTF deployments from the tactical to strategic level. Additionally, Logistics/Mobility Chiefs articulate logistical and strategic mobility requirements to appropriate agencies both inside and outside the Service. Furthermore, assignments to embed within the U.S. Navy as combat cargo assistants (CCAs) aboard naval amphibious warfare ships and within various commands of the Navy. Lastly, Logistics/Mobility Chiefs facilitate unit level logistics and embarkation training within their commands.

provision.label: b.

Must have had previous duty as an 0441 or a 0471 USMCR.

Logistics/Mobility follow-on courses that enhance MOS proficiency are identified in the current version of the MOS Roadmap within the Marine Corps Training Information Management System (MCTIMS). Listed courses outline which course directly contribute to the growth of the 0491.

The completion of listed courses enhances proficiency and increases the probability of Marines being promoted to the next grade. Marines who complete all identified courses will be viewed has highly competitive for promotion and set themselves apart from their peers.

These courses and their completion coincide with requirements identified within the most current version on the Logistics Training and Readiness Manual which contribute to the professional capability of the individual Marine and capacity within the logistics community.

2. MOS 0506, Red Team Member (MGySgt to SSgt) FMOS, DC CD&I

provision.text: MOS 0506, Red Team Member (MGySgt to SSgt) FMOS, DC CD&I

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Red Team Members provide commanders with an independent capability to fully explore alternatives in plans, operations, and capabilities in the context of the operational environment and from the perspective of both our partners and adversaries. They promote staff self- awareness and help frame problems and questions, manage small groups, integrate staff planning, close communication gaps amongst the staff, and help the staff become aware of potential cognitive biases and logic fallacies. Red Team Members serve at Headquarters Marine Corps, Training and Education Command, Marine Corps University, MAGTF Staff Training Program, MEF staffs, MEB staffs and the U.S. Army’s University of Foreign Military and Cultural Studies.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites. Security requirement: adjudicated NACLC secret security clearance with eligibility for access to top secret (TS) and TS- sensitive compartmented information (SCI). 3112 NAVMC 1200.1L 3-55 Enclosure (1)

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements
Complete a course taught by MCU red team instructors that meets army foreign military and cultural studies standard.
MOS will be assigned by EDCOM upon completion of the course.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties
Provide critical reviews and analysis of concepts and plans (classified and unclassified) as well as providing alternative and creative solutions.

Anticipate the cultural perception of partners, adversaries and others by identifying the second and third order effects of operations in a cultural context and anticipating strategic and operational implications.

Improve decision making during planning and operations by assisting in the development of problem definition and desired end states, identifying friendly and enemy vulnerabilities, challenging assumptions and offering alternative perspectives.
Lead Red Teams during OPTs or serve as a facilitator for Red Teaming of special projects, policies, initiatives, or other command-directed activities.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code. None.

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Related Military Skill. None.

section.heading: 3. MOS 0511, MAGTF Planning Specialist (MGySgt to Pvt) PMOS, DC PP&O

provision.text: MOS 0511, MAGTF Planning Specialist (MGySgt to Pvt) PMOS, DC PP&O

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. The Enlisted MAGTF Planning Specialist is responsible for functional support in the areas of Force Deployment Planning & Execution (FDP&E), Joint Combat Capability Assessment (JCCA), and Global Force Management (GFM). Typical duties include updating plan via established GFM/ FDP&E automated data processing tools and coordinating execution of force deployment plans.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Must be a U.S. citizen.
Must possess a CL score of 100 or GT score of 100 or higher.
Security requirement:

provision.label: (a)
provision.text: Must be eligible for a top secret (TS) security clearance and access to Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) predicated on a completed single scope background investigation (SSBI). Application for TS security clearance must be submitted during recruit training or prior to attendance of the MAGTF Planner Basic Course (N46KAG2), MARDET Dam Neck, Virginia Beach, VA.

provision.label: (b)
provision.text: Marines with the MOS 0511 who are re-enlisting must possess an adjudicated Secret security clearance and are required to submit a 3112 NAVMC 1200.1L 3-56 Enclosure (1) application for a top-secret security clearance prior to finalizing their re- enlistment. Interim Secret security clearances shall not be authorized.

provision.label: (c)
provision.text: Marines conducting lateral moves to the 0511 MOS must possess an adjudicated secret security clearance. Upon favorable recommendation from MOS screening interview, lateral move request Marines are required to submit an application for a top-secret security clearance prior to attending the MAGTF Planner Basic Course. Students arriving with interim secret clearances will not be allowed to complete the training.
Lateral moves:

provision.label: (a)
provision.text: Must be worldwide deployable at the time SNM is approved for lateral move into the 0511 MOS and meet criteria for reenlistment set forth in reference (bj).

provision.label: (b)
provision.text: Marines conducting lateral moves to the 0511 MOS must be a Corporal (Maximum 12 months TIG) or below (waiverable by MMEA) in any MOS.

provision.label: (c)
provision.text: All Marines requesting a lateral move into this MOS must have a screening interview conducted by a 0511 MSgt or above. GySgt 0511s at an MSC can conduct interviews if authorized by their respective MEF Plans Chief. Interview waivers may be granted only by the 0511 OccFld Sponsor or CMC.

provision.label: (d)
provision.text: Prior to conducting the lateral move interview, all applicants will read the Force Deployment Planning and Execution (FDP&E) Manual (reference (ch)) and Individual Training Standard for MAGTF Plans/ Operations Officer (MOS 0502) and MAGTF Planning Specialist (MOS 0511) (reference (da)).

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements
Complete the Marine Air-Ground Task Force (MAGTF) Planning Specialist Course (N46KAG2), MARDET Dam Neck, Virginia Beach, VA.

Marines who execute a lateral move to the 0511 MOS must attend PMOS training within 6 months of reporting to a command offering on the job training (OJT), depending on class seat availability. Failure to attend and complete MOS training will result in an MOS reclassification or separation per current MMEA guideline and applicable MCOs.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to reference (aq), MAGTF Planning Training and Readiness Manual.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code. Command and Control Center Specialists 55-3015.

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Related Military Skill
Force Deployment Planning and Execution (FDP&E) Officer, 0502.
Marine Air Ground Task Force (MAGTF) Planners, 0505. 3112 NAVMC 1200.1L 3-57 Enclosure (1)

section.heading: 4. MOS 0522, Psychological Operations (PSYOP) Non-Commissioned Officer

provision.text: MOS 0522, Psychological Operations (PSYOP) Non-Commissioned Officer (MGySgt to Cpl) EMOS (0521), DC I

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. PSYOP Marines plan and execute functions pertaining to military information support operations (MISO). PSYOP is defined as the trained personnel who primarily conduct MISO, but can also, in certain contexts, conduct civil authorities’ information support (CAIS) and military deception (MILDEC). MISO are planned operations to convey selected information and indicators to foreign audiences to influence their emotions, motives, objective reasoning, and, ultimately, the behavior of foreign governments, organizations, groups, and individuals in a manner favorable to the originator objectives. PSYOP capabilities are critical to the success of the marine air ground task force (MAGTF) mission, as they enable commanders to shape the information and security environment in their areas of responsibility (AOR). The active-duty structure for this FMOS has converted to the 1751 PMOS. For the detailed description of the new MOS please reference the PMOS 1751, Influence Specialist. THIS IS AN OBSOLETE MOS, NO LONGER IN USE IN THE TABLE OF ORGANIZATION OF THE MARINE CORPS. THIS MOS IS MAINTAINED IN THE MOS MANUAL BECAUSE IT APPEARS IN THE RECORDS OF MARINES STILL ON ACTIVE DUTY OR THE RESERVES.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Must possess a GT score of 100 or higher.
Security requirement: secret security clearance. SNCOs must be eligible for a TS/SCI.
Currently reside in a 0522 billet or in receipt of orders to fill a 0522 billet.
Must be worldwide deployable prior to executing orders to fill a 0522 billet.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements
Complete the Psychological Operations Specialists Course (A05M301), John F. Kennedy Special Warfare Center and Schools, Ft Liberty, NC.
PSYOP MOS Specialists will assign a Marine the 0522 AMOS upon completion of the above training requirements.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties
Develop MISO plans and advise the commander and staff on the conduct of MISO for all operations, contingencies, and exercises.
Analyze target audiences and evaluate effects of MISO operations; apply MISO techniques and methodology.
Design and develop MISO products.
Coordinate with joint, interagency, and other personnel to meet mission requirements.

Conduct MISO as directed by the commander during all phases of operations as a member of an expeditionary MISO team, expeditionary MISO 3112 NAVMC 1200.1L 3-58 Enclosure (1) detachment, IO support team, MISO planning team, or while serving in a MISO billet on a staff.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code. Military Enlisted Tactical Operations and Air/Weapons Specialists and Crew Members, All Other 55-3019.

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Related Military Skill
Civil Affairs Noncommissioned Officer, 0531.
Civil Affairs Specialist, 0532.
Female Engagement Specialist, 0538.
Civil-Military Operations Chief, 0539.
Information Specialist, 0551.
Advisor, 0570.
Operational Advisor, 0571.

section.heading: 5. MOS 0538, Female Engagement Specialist (MGySgt to Cpl) FMOS, DCI

provision.text: MOS 0538, Female Engagement Specialist (MGySgt to Cpl) FMOS, DCI

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. THIS IS AN OBSOLETE MOS, NO LONGER IN USE IN THE TABLE OF ORGANIZATION OF THE MARINE CORPS. THIS MOS IS MAINTAINED IN THE MOS MANUAL BECAUSE IT APPEARS IN THE RECORDS OF MARINES STILL ON ACTIVE DUTY OR THE RESERVES. Female Engagement Specialists act as an interface between the MAGTF commander and a wide variety of civilian populations, agencies, and organizations. While the majority of their efforts are focused on the female population engagements with male populations are encouraged and often garner more information relevant for mission success.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Must be a Corporal or above.
Security requirement: secret security clearance eligibility.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements
To be awarded the FMOS, Marines must complete requirements (2) and (3) prior to contacting the OccFld manager at MCCMOS.
Complete the Civil Reconnaissance NCO Course (M02AAPD) or the Civil Affairs Specialist Course (M02ZSGD) conducted at MCCMOS, MCB Quantico, VA.
Complete the JKO Course (J3TA-MN1292).

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to reference (aq), MAGTF Planner’s Training and Readiness (T/R) Manual.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code. None. 3112 NAVMC 1200.1L 3-59 Enclosure (1)

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Related Military Skill
Advisor, 0570.
Operational Advisor, 0571.
Influence Specialist, 1751.

section.heading: 6. MOS 0551, Information Specialist (MGySgt to Cpl) FMOS, DC I

provision.text: MOS 0551, Information Specialist (MGySgt to Cpl) FMOS, DC I

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Information Practitioners are focused on the information environment (IE), operational planning and coordination, IE characterization/ analysis, and integration of information. Duties encompass the supervision of tasking, processing, and dissemination of products related to the thirteen

different information related capabilities (IRCs); operation security (OPSEC), military deception (MILDEC), information assurance (IA), cyberspace operations, electronic warfare (EW), special effects, physical attack, physical security, defense support to public diplomacy (DSPD), communications strategy and operations (COMMSTRAT), counterintelligence (CI), civil military operations (CMO), and military information support operations (MISO). Advanced Information Planners prepare and issue reports to include target audience analysis reports, technical reports, and summaries. This MOS will be assigned as a non-PMOS only by the CMC (MM). The active-duty structure for this FMOS has converted to the 1751 PMOS/1781 FMOS. For the detailed description of the new MOS please reference the PMOS 1751, Influence Specialist.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Must possess a GT score of 100 or higher.
Security requirement: secret security clearance.
Must be currently in or have orders to fill an enlisted information planner billet.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements
Complete the MAGTF Operations in the Information Environment Specialist Course (M02F2KD), Quantico, VA.
Any of these requirements may be waived by the Deputy Commandant for Information based on unique work or educational experience.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to reference (aq), MAGTF Planner’s Training and Readiness (T/R) Manual.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code. No civilian equivalent.

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Related Military Skill. None.

section.heading: 7. MOS 0560, Security Cooperation (SC) Planner (MGySgt to Sgt) FMOS, DC PP&O

provision.text: MOS 0560, Security Cooperation (SC) Planner (MGySgt to Sgt) FMOS, DC PP&O

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. SC Planners work closely with operational planners to ensure planned SC engagements enable USMC operations, to include readiness generation and/or sustainment activities for USMC forces, potential prepositioning and access, coalition partner interoperability, and 3112 NAVMC 1200.1L 3-60 Enclosure (1) contribution to deterrence via the development of partner nation defensive capabilities. SC Planners develop multi-year engagement plans in support of overarching global campaign plans, combatant command campaign plans, and other high-level strategic guidance. SC Planners have a comprehensive understanding of the USMC SC planning and execution cycle.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Security requirement: secret clearance required.
Complete the Foundations of Security Cooperation (SC-102) and Introduction to Socium (SOC-101) virtual training courses provided by the Defense Security Cooperation University (DSCU).

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements
Complete the Security Cooperation Planners Course (SCPC) (N030JX3 or N030JXM) provided by Security Cooperation Training Detachment, Marine Corps Intelligence Schools.
MOS 0560 will be assigned by the Marine's O-5 level or above commanding officer upon completion of Security Cooperation Planners Course.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties. Supports SC planners in assessing, monitoring, and evaluating SC activities and use of SC authorities, and conducts research in support of the development of SC engagement plans, and/or engagement plans.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code. None.

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Related Military Skill
Operational Planner, 0505.
Advanced Information Operations Planner, 0550.
Advisor, 0570.
Operational Advisor, 0571.
Civil Military Operations Planner, 1708.

section.heading: 8. MOS 0570, Advisor (SgtMaj/MGySgt to Sgt) FMOS, DC PP&O

provision.text: MOS 0570, Advisor (SgtMaj/MGySgt to Sgt) FMOS, DC PP&O

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Advisors have general knowledge acquired from the formal military learning center (FMLC) training and meet the minimum knowledge, skills, and abilities defined in the Security Cooperation Training and Readiness Manual. An Advisor understands advisor techniques and is capable of developing a foreign counterpart and persuading them to achieve U.S. government (USG), service, and partner nation security objectives. Marine Advisors are proficient in their primary MOS or other unique skills. They are familiar with language, regional expertise, and culture (LREC). They can analyze the operational environment and understand the influence of culture, build and maintain relationships and rapport with counterparts, or other Marine Corps security assistance missions (e.g., stability operations, civil affairs, liaison, Stand in Forces, etc.) to further mission objectives. Advisors recognize and mitigate cultural stress, develop and implement training plans and events to build capability or capacity, participate in 3112 NAVMC 1200.1L 3-61 Enclosure (1) security cooperation planning, are able to employ force protection skills (as required by the combatant commander and/or chief of mission), and understand USG and service objectives and plans for an assigned region or country.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites. Security requirement: secret level clearance eligibility.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements. Complete the Marine Advisor Course (N03KYK3 or N03KYKM) provided by the Security Cooperation Training Detachment, Marine Corps Intelligence Schools. Exceptions may be granted for equivalent service/joint/NATO/interagency advisor formalized training by the occupational field manager, HQMC (PLU).

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to reference (ci), Security Cooperation/Language Regional Expertise and Culture Training and Readiness (T&R) Manual.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code. None.

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Related Military Skill. Security Cooperation Planner, 0560.

section.heading: 9. MOS 0571, Operational Advisor (SgtMaj/MGySgt to Sgt) FMOS, DC PP&O

provision.text: MOS 0571, Operational Advisor (SgtMaj/MGySgt to Sgt) FMOS, DC PP&O

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Operational Advisors must first be qualified in their primary MOS or other unique skill. Operational Advisors can translate expertise and experiences into useful advice to develop a foreign counterpart and persuade them to achieve U.S. Government (USG), service, and partner nation security objectives. They analyze the operational environment and understand the influence of culture, build, and maintain relationships with counterparts, or conduct other Marine Corps tasks and operations (e.g., stability operations, civil affairs, liaison, Stand in Forces, etc.) to further mission objectives. Operational Advisors recognize and mitigate cultural stress, develop, and implement training plans and events to build capability or capacity, participate in security cooperation planning, possess force protection skills (as required by the combatant commander and/or chief of mission), and understand USG and Service objectives and plans for an assigned region or country. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to the Security Cooperation Training and Readiness Manual.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Security requirement: secret level clearance.
Must be complete in current rank with Regional and Culture Studies Program training per in accordance with MARADMIN 348-19/191951Z JUN 19 and MARADMIN 227-20/081529Z APR 20).
Have completed the Marine Advisor Course (N03KYK or N03KYKM ). Exceptions may be granted for equivalent service/joint/NATO/interagency advisor formalized training.

provision.label: (a)
provision.text: Marines possessing these MOSs must complete of one or more deployments with a Special Operations unit or as an individual augment to a Joint Special Operations unit for a cumulative period of no less than six months. 3112 NAVMC 1200.1L 3-62 Enclosure (1)

provision.label: (b)
provision.text: The Marine Advisor Course is not required for Marines possessing one of the following primary MOSs 0372, Marine Raider, 0370, Marine Raider Officer, or necessary MOS 8071, Special Operations Capability Specialist.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements

Effective with the release of MARADMIN 522-20, Commanding Officers at the O-5 level and above may now approve the 0571 FMOS for Marines who have met the prerequisites contained in paragraph 12.b above and demonstrated extensive knowledge and expertise in advising in an on-the-job operational environment, encompassing a period of no less than six months. Commanding Officers shall review fitness reports and other source documents (e.g., deployment orders, awards) to determine eligibility of the Marine and ensure the Marine was assigned to an advisor billet and daily performing the duties identified in paragraph 12.d. below.
Advisor skills are perishable and therefore the experience must be within the last seven years to qualify.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to reference (ci), Security Cooperation/Language Regional Expertise and Culture Training and Readiness (T&R) Manual.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code. None.

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Related Military Skill. Security Cooperation Planner, 0560.

section.heading: 10. MOS 0577, Operations and Tactics Instructor (MGySgt to MSgt) NMOS (0321,

provision.text: MOS 0577, Operations and Tactics Instructor (MGySgt to MSgt) NMOS (0321, 0393, 0399, 0848, 1371, 1833, 1869), DC PP&O

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Operations and Tactics Instructors assist with the planning and execution of the Unit Readiness Program, the conduct of operational planning and the execution of operations across the range of military operations for regimental and battalion sized units. Additionally, SNCOs with this MOS can be utilized during later tours in their career to fill Operations Chief Billets for higher level staffs, or to fill appropriate joint and service level billets requiring training, planning and operational expertise. This MOS will be assigned as a NMOS only.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites. Security requirement: secret level clearance.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements. Completion of the Operations and Tactics Instructor Chief Course (M09HE35).

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties. See MCWP 3-11.5 Marine Infantry Battalion and MCWP 3-1 Ground Combat Operations.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code. None.

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Related Military Skill. None. 3112 NAVMC 1200.1L 3-63 Enclosure (1)

section.heading: 11. MOS 0580, Foreign Disclosure Representative (FDR) (MGySgt to SSgt) FMOS,

provision.text: MOS 0580, Foreign Disclosure Representative (FDR) (MGySgt to SSgt) FMOS, DC PP&O

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Foreign Disclosure Representative (FDR) are officially designated in writing by a command, unit, or agency with delegated disclosure authority to regulate disclosures of classified military information (CMI), controlled unclassified information (CUI), technology, and equipment to foreign nationals/organizations in accordance with applicable policies. FDRs require training in foreign disclosure policy, considerations, and strategies to protect national security interests and strengthen relations with foreign allies. DC PP&O will assign this MOS as an FMOS.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites. Security requirement: minimum of secret clearance. The primary command FDO requires a T5 or T5R investigation.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements
Complete the Marine Corps Foreign Disclosure Officer Course (SSC: OB2), managed by PP&O.
If it is determined an officer cannot reasonably serve instead, receive an appointment letter as an FDO from the commander or head of an organization with delegated disclosure authority.
Recommended additional training:

provision.label: (a)
provision.text: Defense Intelligence Enterprise Foreign Disclosure Officer Course (DIA-INT-2300).

provision.label: (b)
provision.text: Security Cooperation Workforce Basic Level Certification.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties
Establishes and maintains the commands foreign disclosure program in accordance with MCO 5510.20C.

Applies foreign disclosure policy, best practices, and training in determining information, training, technology, equipment, and capabilities to be shared with foreign governments, entities, and non-governmental and international organizations.
Plans and reviews foreign nationals’ access to information, equipment, and capabilities during visits.
Prepares delegation of disclosure authority letters guiding U.S. personnel interaction with foreign nationals during training, exercises, operations, and programs.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code. None.

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Related Military Skill. None. 3113 NAVMC 1200.1L 3-64 Enclosure (1) 3113. OCCUPATIONAL FIELD 06, COMMUNICATIONS

section.heading: 1. Introduction. The Communications Occupational Field (OccFld) includes
2. MOS 0621, Transmissions System Operator (Sgt to Pvt) PMOS, DIR IC4

provision.text: MOS 0621, Transmissions System Operator (Sgt to Pvt) PMOS, DIR IC4

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Transmissions System Operators employ transmissions systems to enable essential warfighting functions including Intelligence, Fires, Logistics, Information, Command and Control (C2), Force Protection, and Maneuver capabilities to support activities across Department of Defense (DoD) operational domains. Their responsibilities encompass installation, operation, and maintenance of single and dual channel radio including vehicular and man-pack systems, and Multi-Channel Line of Sight (LOS) systems operating in HF, VHF, UHF, and SHF bands, establishing over-the-air (OTA) transmission links between a multitude of distant stations, message traffic management, information flow, and dissemination and implementation of authorized changes to network parameters, encryption protocols, and transmissions security; planning, coordinating, and executing operations using program of record and commercial-of-the-shelf (COTS) equipment and field-expedient antennas for network integration, proficiency with specialized computer hardware/software planning tools, Transmission Security (TRANSEC), and Communications Security (COMSEC), and are familiar with spectrum analyzing tools and DoD approved Position Navigation and Timing (PNT) devices. Operators may be assigned to Billet Identification Codes (BIC) within their field, associated with DoD Cyber Workforce Framework (DCWF) work role codes. Additional training and certification requirements 3113 NAVMC 1200.1L 3-65 Enclosure (1) related to these codes are outlined in DoDI 8140.10, DoDM 8140.10, and the MOS roadmap.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Must be a U.S. citizen.
Must have normal color vision.
Security requirement: secret security clearance eligibility.
Must possess a CL score of 100 or EL score of 100 or higher.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements
Complete the Basic Communications Course, (M09KJT1).
Complete the Narrowband Terrestrial System Operator Course (M0925U1) at Marine Corps Communications-Electronics School, at Twentynine Palms, CA.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to reference (i), Communications Training and Readiness Manual.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code. See Marine Corps Cool Program: http://www.cool.navy.mil/usmc.

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Related Military Skill
Space Planning and Waveform Integration Officer, 0620.
Satellite Transmissions Operator, 0627.
Transmissions System Chief, 0629.
Spectrum Manager 0648.

section.heading: 3. MOS 0623, Troposcatter Transmissions System Operator (Sgt to Pvt) NMOS

provision.text: MOS 0623, Troposcatter Transmissions System Operator (Sgt to Pvt) NMOS (0621), DIR IC4

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Troposcatter Transmissions System Operators install, operate and maintain tropospheric transmissions systems to enable command and control. Marines will operate complex transmission systems to integrate communication networks. Operators will be familiar with spectrum analyzing tools, specialized computer hardware/software programs, transmission security (TRANSEC), and communications security (COMSEC). Skill progression training for staff sergeant through corporal is the Transmissions Supervisor Course located at Camp Pendleton (M10BNPB), Camp Lejeune (M03BNPG), and Okinawa (M22BNP4) at the Regional Communications Training Centers.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites. Must possess MOS 0621.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements. Complete the Wideband Terrestrial Transmission System Operator Course (M09DRW1) at Twentynine Palms, CA.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to reference (i), Communications Training and Readiness Manual. 3113 NAVMC 1200.1L 3-66 Enclosure (1)

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code. See Marine Corps Cool Program: http://www.cool.navy.mil/usmc.

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Related Military Skill. Transmissions System Chief, 0629.

section.heading: 4. MOS 0627, Satellite Transmissions System Operator (Sgt to Pvt) PMOS, DIR

provision.text: MOS 0627, Satellite Transmissions System Operator (Sgt to Pvt) PMOS, DIR IC4

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Satellite Transmissions System Operators employ Wideband Satellite Communications (SATCOM) and Troposcatter Transmissions Systems to enable essential warfighting functions including intelligence, fires, logistics, information, command and control (C2), force protection, and maneuver capabilities to support activities across Department of Defense (DoD) operational domains. Their responsibilities encompass installation, operation, and maintenance of Wideband SATCOM and Troposcatter Transmissions systems operating in the L, C, X, KU, KA, and EHF bands, proficiency with spectrum analyzing tools, specialized computer hardware/software planning tools, transmission security (TRANSEC), and communications security (COMSEC), familiar with DoD approved position navigation and timing (PNT) devices. Operators may be assigned to billet identification codes (BIC) within their field, associated with DoD Cyber Workforce Framework (DCWF) work role codes. Additional training and certification requirements related to these codes are outlined in DoDI 8140.10, DoDM 8140.10, and the MOS roadmap.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Must be a U.S. citizen.
Must have normal color vision.
Security requirement: secret security clearance eligibility.
Must possess a CL score of 100 or EL score of 100 or higher.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements
Complete the Basic Communications Course, (M09KJT1).
Complete the Wideband Satellite Communication System Operator Course (M09DR31), Communication Training Battalion, Twentynine Palms, CA.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to reference (i), Communications Training and Readiness Manual.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code. See Marine Corps Cool Program: http://www.cool.navy.mil/usmc.

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Related Military Skill
Space Planning and Waveform Integration Officer, 0620.
Transmissions System Operator, 0621.
Transmissions Chief, 0629.
Spectrum Manager, 0648. 3113 NAVMC 1200.1L 3-67 Enclosure (1)
Intelligence Surveillance Reconnaissance (ISR) Systems Engineer, 2651.

section.heading: 5. MOS 0628, Tactical Transmission Systems Operator Maintainer (Sgt to Pvt)

provision.text: MOS 0628, Tactical Transmission Systems Operator Maintainer (Sgt to Pvt) NMOS (0627), DIR IC4

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Tactical Transmission Systems Operator Maintainers install, operate, and maintain various wideband satellite communication terminals operating in the AEHF band. Marines will be trained to operate the secure mobile anti-jam reliable tactical terminals (SMART-T) to integrate communication networks and enable command and control. Operators will be familiar with spectrum analyzing tools, specialized computer hardware/ software programs, transmission security (TRANSEC), and communications security (COMSEC). Skill progression training for sergeant through corporal is the Transmissions Supervisor Course located at Camp Pendleton (M10BNPB), Camp Lejeune (M03BNPG), and Okinawa (M22BNP4) at the regional communications training centers.

section.heading: 6. MOS 0629, Transmissions Chief (GySgt to SSgt) PMOS, DIR IC4

provision.text: MOS 0629, Transmissions Chief (GySgt to SSgt) PMOS, DIR IC4

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Transmissions Chiefs oversee advanced transmissions operations, including planning, installation, operation, maintenance, and supervision to enable essential warfighting functions including intelligence, fires, logistics, information, command and control (C2), force protection, and maneuver capabilities to support activities across Department of Defense (DoD) operational domains. Their responsibilities encompass development of site plans for single and dual channel radio, terrestrial wideband transmission systems (TWTS), and wideband satellite communications (SATCOM) systems, maintenance of single and dual channel radio including vehicular and man-pack systems, TWTS, and wideband SATCOM systems operating in HF, VHF, UHF, SHF, and EHF bands, integrate critical transmission planning data into 3113 NAVMC 1200.1L 3-68 Enclosure (1) communications electronic operating instructions (CEOI), management of training, security measures, and equipment deployment, ensuring systems integration across transmissions elements, data communications, wireless architecture, and cybersecurity; utilizing programming and planning tools, implementing and overseeing proper execution of maintenance procedures, and handling budgeting and administrative processes. Marines may be assigned to billet identification codes (BIC) within their field, associated with DoD cyber workforce framework (DCWF) work role codes. Additional training and certification requirements related to these codes are outlined in DoDI 8140.10, DoDM 8140.10, and the MOS roadmap.

section.heading: 7. MOS 0631, Network Administrator (Sgt to Pvt) PMOS, DIR IC4

provision.text: MOS 0631, Network Administrator (Sgt to Pvt) PMOS, DIR IC4

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Network Administrators install operate and maintain local area networks (LAN) and wide area networks (WAN) to enable command and control. Typical duties include routing/switching configuration, cybersecurity, premise wiring, installation of network components. They establish technical control sites, conduct fault analysis, circuit testing and end to end troubleshooting. Additional responsibilities include network monitoring and quality of service (QOS) to maintain adequate bandwidth utilization in of communication networks and data services. Network Administrators will maintain records on activation/deactivation of communications links and maintenance actions performed. Marines will be familiar with routing protocols, virtual private networks (VPN), internet protocol security (IPSEC), subnetting, traffic monitoring and cybersecurity. Skill progression training for staff sergeant through corporal is the Network Supervisor Course located at Camp Pendleton (M10BNPB), Camp Lejeune (M03BNPG), and Okinawa (M22BNP4) at the Regional Communications Training Centers. Marines in this MOS may be assigned to a BIC within their occupational field that has been coded with one or more DoD Cyber Workforce Framework (DCWF) work role codes. Please reference DoDI 8140.10, DoDM 8140.10, and the MOS roadmap for additional training and certification requirements associated with these work role codes.

Must possess a CL score of 105 or EL score of 105 or higher.

Complete the Network Administrator Course (M09CVS1) at Twentynine Palms, CA.

provision.text: Summary. Network Chiefs install, operate, maintain, and supervise local area networks (LAN) and wide area networks (WAN) to enable command and control. Additionally, Network Chiefs must be thoroughly familiar with security, programming and planning tools, maintenance procedures, budgeting, and administration processes. Network Chiefs also supervise the establishment of the technical control sites. section.heading: 10. MOS 0648, Electromagnetic Spectrum Management Chief (MSgt to Sgt) NMOS

provision.text: MOS 0648, Electromagnetic Spectrum Management Chief (MSgt to Sgt) NMOS (0621, 0627, 0629, 0699), DIR IC4

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Spectrum Manager coordinates, manages, and de-conflicts the use of electromagnetic spectrum (EMS) and spectrum dependent systems (SDS) ISO Marine Air Ground Task Force (MAGTF), joint, and coalition forces. Electromagnetic Spectrum Management Chiefs support electromagnetic spectrum operations (EMSO) by conducting and providing input from the electromagnetic spectrum management operations interrelated functions of frequency management, host nation coordination, and interference reporting. Electromagnetic Spectrum Management Chiefs must be thoroughly familiar with and trained in international, national, DOD, joint and service level spectrum policy, allocations, and frequency assignment procedures; spectrum supportability and certification procedures, coordination of host nation approval (HNA), radio theory, spectrum analysis and engineering effects of electromagnetic compatibility (EMC), and determination, mitigation and resolution of electromagnetic interference (EMI). Electromagnetic Spectrum Management Chiefs implement policy and guidance for the effective and efficient use of the electromagnetic spectrum, administer and manage the MAGTF's use of national level and DOD associated spectrum databases, and coordinates the development of the command and control (C2) communications instructions (currently-CEOI) and joint restricted frequency list (JRFL) and ensures requirements are implemented into the EMSO Plan. Electromagnetic Spectrum Management Chiefs must be knowledgeable of the spectrum management process supporting all DOD/Service and commercial SDS. 3113 NAVMC 1200.1L 3-72 Enclosure (1)

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Must be a U.S. citizen.
Must possess a GT score of 105 or higher and CL score of 105 or higher.
Security requirement: top secret with sensitive compartmented information access eligibility.

Must have obtained the rank of sergeant or above in one of the following MOSs 0621, 0627, 0629, 0699, or 5948. 06XX Sgt's must have completed the Transmissions Supervisor Course located at Camp Pendleton (M10BNPB), Camp Lejeune (M03BNPG), or Okinawa (M22BNP4) at the Regional Communications Training Centers.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements
Complete the Electromagnetic Spectrum Management Course (F0224L1) Biloxi, MS.
Active-duty Marines must have 24 months obligated service remaining upon graduation from the MOS producing school.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to reference (i), Communications Training and Readiness Manual.

provision.text: Summary. Data Systems Administrators support a myriad of computer and Network Operating Systems (NOS) to include versions of Linux, Microsoft, and Unix, to enable command and control. Typical duties include active directory administration, domain name service (DNS) public key infrastructure (PKI), warfighting systems, cybersecurity, database administration and unified communications. section.heading: 14. MOS 0681, Information Security Technician (MGySgt to SSgt) PMOS, DIR IC4

provision.text: MOS 0681, Information Security Technician (MGySgt to SSgt) PMOS, DIR IC4 #

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Information Security Technicians (IST) serves as the Marine Corps primary functional proponent for the Department of the Navy's (DoN) Communications Security (COMSEC) and cryptographic key management. These Marines provide day-to-day operation of the DoN's COMSEC material control system (CMCS). The duties include coordinate for the provisioning of symmetric and asymmetric key products to support C4 systems in collaboration with communications planners for the development of communications instructions and support for elements of the Marine Air Ground Task Force (MAGTF) or other authorized elements requiring authorized support, provide information regarding new or revised COMSEC policies and procedures and their impact on the command, train and inspect COMSEC users within the command, monitors and maintains the command COMSEC material allowances performs spot checks of users to assess adherence to prescribed instructions. Also, may serve as a Central Office of Record (COR) Auditor for COMSEC account inspections. Lateral move into this MOS may be from any MOS at the grade of staff sergeant. This MOS will be awarded to Marines approved for lateral move upon completion of one of the listed approved courses in subparagraph

section.heading: 15. MOS 0699, Communications Chief (MGySgt to MSgt) PMOS, DIR IC4

provision.text: MOS 0699, Communications Chief (MGySgt to MSgt) PMOS, DIR IC4

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Communications Chief must possess thorough understanding of equipment capabilities and system integration for all elements of transmissions, networks, data systems, cybersecurity, information, and communications security management. They are trained to evaluate technical supportability and limitations of communications equipment, draft systems 3113 NAVMC 1200.1L 3-77 Enclosure (1) architecture, communications plans, and coordinate technical interface and restoration issues with higher, adjacent, and subordinate commands. Additionally, they are responsible for manpower management, training, equipment accountability, and operational readiness. The Communications Chief can serve as the Senior Enlisted Advisor (SEA) to the Director of Command, Control, Communications and Computers (C4), Headquarters Marine Corps and at the Marine Corps Cyberspace Operations Group (MCCOG), occupational field specialist on the staff of HQMC C4, and as communications chiefs for communication training battalion, at the MARFOR level, and in all levels of the Marine Air-Ground Task Force (MAGTF). The duties of the Communications Chief encompass providing assistance and advice to MAGTF Commanders AC/S G-6, Commanders of Communication Battalions, and other designated commands concerning plans, policies, procedures and emerging communications requirements and capabilities led by HQMC C4 and other proponents and advocates. Marines in this MOS may be assigned to a BIC (within their occupational field) that has been coded with one or more DoD Cyber Workforce Framework (DCWF) work role codes. Please reference DoDI 8140.10, DoDM 8140.10, and the MOS roadmap for additional training and certification requirements associated with these work role codes.

section.heading: 1. Introduction. The Field Artillery OccFld is divided among three
2. MOS 0811, Field Artillery Cannoneer (SSgt to Pvt) PMOS, DC PP&O

provision.text: MOS 0811, Field Artillery Cannoneer (SSgt to Pvt) PMOS, DC PP&O

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. As a member of a Field Artillery Howitzer Battery, Cannoneers prepare artillery pieces and equipment for movement, combat, and firing. They inspect and prepare ammunition for firing and perform the various jobs incident to firing such as, laying for elevation and deflection, loading the piece, and handling ammunition. Field Artillery Cannoneers perform preventive maintenance and clean artillery pieces and equipment. They make routine tests and authorize repairs to equipment. Camouflage position, protect equipment from chemical warfare agents, and construct field fortifications.

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. As a member of a HIMARS Battery, Operators prepare the HIMARS for movement, combat, and firing. They inspect and prepare the launcher system for employment to include movement to and from concealment positions and firing positions, operate the fire control systems, and handle multiple launch rocket system (MLRS) family of munitions (MFOM). HIMARS Operators perform preventative maintenance and clean system components. They make routine tests and authorized repairs to HIMARS. They provide security, camouflage positions, and protect HIMARS from chemical warfare agents. This MOS will be assigned by the CMC (MM).

provision.text: MOS 0842, Field Artillery Radar Operator (Sgt to Pvt) PMOS, DC PP&O

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Field Artillery Radar Operators perform the duties required to emplace, operate, and displace counterfire radar systems. Other duties include operating military vehicles, generator assets, communications equipment, establishing radio networks for voice and digital communications, and performing hasty survey techniques. Radar Operators also work in the artillery target processing centers. These duties include operating fire support systems that process counterfire/artillery target intelligence and manage radar assets in the field.

Must meet MOS-specific physical standards (MSPS), as listed in NAVMC 3500.7 prior to graduating from the MOS school.
Must meet initial strength test standards associated with PEF assignments as listed in the glossary (pg. xiv) prior to shipping to recruit training.

section.heading: 5. MOS 0844, Field Artillery Fire Control Marine (Sgt to Pvt) PMOS, DC PP&O

provision.text: MOS 0844, Field Artillery Fire Control Marine (Sgt to Pvt) PMOS, DC PP&O

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Field Artillery Fire Control Marine perform duties essential to the delivery of accurate artillery fire. Typical duties include 3114 NAVMC 1200.1L 3-81 Enclosure (1) preparation of fire control equipment for movement and operation, performance of preventive maintenance, routine testing, authorized minor repairs and fire control equipment, and operation of field communications equipment. Fire control computation includes the use of computer equipment systems, plotting survey data on firing charts, determination of target coordinates, and the conversion to target coordinates and observer's reports into firing data and commands. MOS 0844 is assigned upon completion of formal school. Upon promotion to staff sergeant and the appropriate formal school, the 0844 will be designated MOS 0848.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Must be a U.S. citizen.
Must possess a CL score of 105 or GT score of 105 or higher.
Security requirement: secret security clearance eligibility.
Must meet MOS classification standards as listed in the glossary (pg. xiv) prior to graduating from recruit training.
Must meet MOS-specific physical standards (MSPS), as listed in NAVMC 3500.7 prior to graduating from the MOS school.
Must meet initial strength test standards associated with PEF assignments as listed in the glossary (pg. xiv) prior to shipping to recruit training.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements
Complete the Field Artillery Fire Control Marine Course (A200811), Ft Sill, OK.
This MOS will be retained as an additional MOS upon promotion to staff sergeant in MOS 0848.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to reference (k), Artillery Training and Readiness (T&R) Manual.

section.heading: 6. MOS 0847, Field Artillery Sensor Support Marine (Sgt to Pvt) PMOS, DC

provision.text: MOS 0847, Field Artillery Sensor Support Marine (Sgt to Pvt) PMOS, DC PP&O

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Field Artillery Sensor Support Marines assist in the delivery of accurate artillery fires and prosecution of counter fire fight by developing weather data for artillery ballistic computations, performing survey operation. Duties include preparing and operating weather observation equipment such as theodolites and surface sensors, measuring atmospheric readings, preparing and operating survey equipment such as inertial navigation systems, global positioning system receivers, theodolites and electronic distance measuring equipment. Additionally, the 0847 will prepare and operate acoustic sensors for employment. Other duties include operating computer systems for computations, digital communications, command and control, and imagery development. MOS 0847 is assigned upon completion of 3114 NAVMC 1200.1L 3-82 Enclosure (1) formal school. Upon promotion to Staff Sergeant and the appropriate formal school, the 0847 will be designated MOS 0848.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Must be a U.S. citizen.
Must possess a GT score of 100 or MM score of 100 or higher.
Security requirement: secret security clearance eligibility.
Must meet MOS classification standards as listed in the glossary (pg. xiv) prior to graduating from recruit training.
Must meet MOS-specific physical standards (MSPS), as listed in NAVMC 3500.7 prior to graduating from the MOS school.
Must meet initial strength test standards associated with PEF assignments as listed in the glossary (pg. xiv) prior to shipping to recruit training.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements. Complete the Marine Artillery Sensor Support Marine Course (A20DPZ1), Ft Sill, OK.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to reference (k), Artillery Training and Readiness (T&R) Manual.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code. Artillery Missile and Crewmember 55-3014.

provision.label: f.

section.heading: 7. MOS 0848, Field Artillery Operations Chief (MGySgt to SSgt) PMOS, DC PP&O

provision.text: MOS 0848, Field Artillery Operations Chief (MGySgt to SSgt) PMOS, DC PP&O

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Field Artillery Operations Chief perform the various duties associated with the operation of a field artillery and mortar fire direction center, operations or training section, artillery sensor section, survey section. Duties include preparing personnel and equipment for movement and operation, assisting in location of fire direction center in the field, maintaining a situation map, operations journal, and survey records, performing duties incident to the preparation, reproduction, and distribution of operations orders, training orders, memoranda, schedules, status reports, and S-3 periodic reports, preparing operations maps and overlays, assisting in the establishment and operation of artillery meteorological stations, direct atmospheric meteorological observation interpreting, evaluating and distributing atmospheric data, performing duties incident to execution of sensor plans essential to proper employment of field artillery, assisting in installation, orientation, operation, and maintaining target acquisition radar equipment, and training personnel in radar, meteorological, survey, acoustic, and fire direction procedures.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Must possess a GT score of 105 or higher.
Security requirement: secret security clearance eligibility. 3114 NAVMC 1200.1L

section.heading: 8. MOS 0861, Fire Support Marine (Sgt to Pvt) PMOS, DC PP&O

provision.text: MOS 0861, Fire Support Marine (Sgt to Pvt) PMOS, DC PP&O

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Fire Support Marines perform duties related to the planning, observation, conduct, and control of surface to surface and air to surface fires. These duties include planning, calling for, integrating, coordinating, observing and adjusting artillery (cannon, rocket, missile) and naval surface fire support (NSFS), employment of LASER designators, range finders, and LASER guided munitions and coordination of non-lethal fires. These duties also include operating communications equipment, establishing radio networks for voice and digital communications, as well as operating Marine Corps fire support systems. Upon promotion to staff sergeant and completion of the appropriate formal schools, the 0861 will be designated MOS 0871.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites

Must meet initial strength test standards associated with PEF assignments as listed in the glossary (pg. xiv) prior to shipping to recruit training.

provision.text: Requirements
Complete the Fire Support Marine Course (A20L9T1), Ft Sill, OK.
This MOS will be retained as an additional MOS upon promotion to staff sergeant in MOS 0871.

provision.text: Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to reference (k), Artillery Training and Readiness (T&R) Manual.

section.heading: 9. MOS 0869, Artillery Unit Leader (MGySgt to GySgt) PMOS, DC PP&O

provision.text: MOS 0869, Artillery Unit Leader (MGySgt to GySgt) PMOS, DC PP&O

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. The Artillery Senior Cannoneer is responsible to the commander and assists in the planning, training, deployment and employment of all organic weapons systems and the units combat power capabilities. They supervise and coordinate the preparation and assignment of personnel/ equipment in accordance with the table of organization/table of equipment. Gunnery Sergeants serve as the battery gunnery sergeant/ammunition platoon sergeant (HIMARS). Master Sergeants serve as battery (HIMARS) and battalion field artillery chiefs. Master Gunnery Sergeants serve as battalion (HIMARS) and regimental field artillery chiefs.

section.heading: 10. MOS 0871, Joint Fires and Effects Integrator (MGySgt to SSgt) PMOS, DC

provision.text: MOS 0871, Joint Fires and Effects Integrator (MGySgt to SSgt) PMOS, DC PP&O

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Fires and Effects Integrator serves as the senior enlisted tactical advisor to the commander and staff for all lethal and non-lethal fire support assets to include mortars, artillery (cannon, rocket, missile), NSFS, and provide terminal attack control of fixed and rotary wing aircraft in support of close air support (CAS). These duties include planning, integrating, coordinating, observing Surface to surface fires, employment of LASER designators, range finders. These duties also include operating communications equipment, establishing radio networks for voice and digital communications, as well as operating Marine Corps fire support systems.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Security requirement: secret security clearance required.
Have held MOS 0861, Fire Support Marine for a minimum of 2 years .
Must be certified Joint Terminal Attack Controller (JTAC 8002 NMOS).

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements
Must complete the Tactical Air Control Party (TACP) Course (N036741, N306741) at EWTG. This requirement is not applicable to the Marine Corps Reserve.
Must Complete the Marine Corps Fire Support Chief Course (A20ANY1) at Ft Sill, OK.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to reference (k), Artillery Training and Readiness (T&R) Manual and TACP T&R Manual.

section.heading: 13. MOS 0875, Joint Terminal Attack Controller Instructor (SSgt) NMOS

provision.text: MOS 0875, Joint Terminal Attack Controller Instructor (SSgt) NMOS (0871), DC PP&O POG-70

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Qualified JTAC-Is will be designated by their commanding officer to supervise JTACs and FACs trainees during all phases of JTAC training when that trainee is conducting simulated, dry or live terminal attack control. Per reference (a) non-JTAC certified instructors may instruct JTAC or FAC trainees on course topics which support CAS operations but are not directly associated with controlling of aircraft (examples fire support coordination measures, airspace management, and theater air-ground system). JTAC-Is will also supervise JTACs and FACs during any refresher syllabus found in paragraph five of this Order.

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Qualified JTAC-Es will be designated by their Commanding Officer to conduct initial and recurring 18-month JTAC evaluations. JTAC-Es will serve as the unit level CAS Subject Matter Expert (SME). The JTAC-E will be able to oversee the unit’s TACP program by conducting 18 month evaluations on all JTAC-Es, JTAC-Is, JTACs, and FACs as well as creating and supervising the training of the JTAC-Is within the command.

section.heading: 15. MOS 0877, Weapons and Tactics Instructor-Tactical Air Control Party

provision.text: MOS 0877, Weapons and Tactics Instructor-Tactical Air Control Party Program Manager (MGySgt to GySgt) NMOS (0871), DC PP&O POG-70

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. This MOS requires formal Air Officers instruction, training, and certification. It forms the foundation skill for assignment as a TACP Program Manager, JTAC E, and JTAC-I. A Weapons and Tactics Instructor-TACP Program Manager directs and controls close air support missions and advises commanders of ground units on matters pertaining to air support. In addition, this individual is responsible to the commander for directing and managing a units tactical air control party personnel and training plan.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Must be a U.S. citizen.
Must possess a GT score of 100 or higher.
Must hold MOS 0871, Joint Fires and Effects Integrator.
Security requirement: secret security clearance eligibility.
Must have normal color vision, and vision correctable to 20/20.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements. Must successfully complete the MAWTS-1 Air Officer Course (M140E11), MCAS, Yuma, AZ.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties
Manage a unit’s weapons and tactics training program. 3114 NAVMC 1200.1L 3-90 Enclosure (1)
Perform academic, simulation, and operational instruction on all facets of aviation integration.
Serve as the ground commander’s primary advisor on aviation integration.
Analyze performance and provide corrective guidance to members of a unit’s tactical air control party.
Instruct on current enemy capabilities and the tactics to counter their threat.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code. Teachers and Instructors, All Other 25-3099.

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Related Military Skill
Fire Support Marine, 0861.
Joint Fires and Effects Integrator, 0871. 3115 NAVMC 1200.1L 3-91 Enclosure (1) 3115. OCCUPATIONAL FIELD 09, TRAINING

section.heading: 1. Introduction. Occupational Field 09, Training, comprises MOSs used to
2. MOS 0911, Drill Instructor (SgtMaj/MGySgt to Sgt) EMOS, CG TECOM

provision.text: MOS 0911, Drill Instructor (SgtMaj/MGySgt to Sgt) EMOS, CG TECOM

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Drill Instructors supervise, instruct, or assist in commanding and instructing a recruit platoon. Once voided, this MOS may not be reassigned without prior approval from the CMC (MM).

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites. Must be screened and meet the prerequisites prescribed in the current Marine Corps order that pertains to the selecting, screening, and preparing enlisted marines for screenable billets and independent duty assignments (SCREENMAN) MCO 1326.6 CH1.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements. At the master sergeant to sergeant level, complete Drill Instructor School (M0681E2), Parris Island, SC or (M0881E2), MCRD San Diego, CA.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties
Instructs and assists in training basic combat tasks to recruits.
Trains recruits in the fundamentals of service life and the- development in the recruit of discipline, physical fitness, pride, and love of the Marine Corps and country.
Trains recruits in close order drill.
Instructs in nomenclature, disassembly, assembly, and functioning of small arms and assists in marksmanship instruction.
Instructs in general orders for sentinels, interior guard duty, personal hygiene, first aid, military bearing and neatness, and care of clothing and equipment.
Lectures on Marine Corps history and tradition, customs of the service, military courtesy, and U.S. Navy Regulations.
Assists in conduct of parades, reviews, and bayonet drill.
Maintains records and prepares reports.
Conducts recruit training for newly enlisted personnel following the recruit training schedules and orders.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code. Teachers and Instructors, All Other 25-3099. 3115 NAVMC 1200.1L 3-92 Enclosure (1)

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Related Military Skill. Marksmanship Instructor, 0931.

section.heading: 3. MOS 0913, Marine Combat Instructor (GySgt to Cpl) EMOS (0311, 0313, 0321,

provision.text: MOS 0913, Marine Combat Instructor (GySgt to Cpl) EMOS (0311, 0313, 0321, 0331, 0341, 0352, 0363, 0369), CG TECOM

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. The Marine Combat Instructor instructs and assists in the training of basic combat skills to entry level Marines to include weapons handling, automatic weapons, munitions, combat conditioning, land navigation, communications, offensive/defensive tactics and scouting/patrolling. The Marine Combat Instructor reinforces core values instilled in recruit training by setting the superior example with professional conduct, knowledge, bearing, attitude, and provides student performance counseling.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Must meet the prerequisites prescribed in MCO 1326.6 CH 1.
Must meet the standards screening checklist of special assignments per MCO 1326.6 CH 1.
Must meet Marine Corps height, weight, and body fat standards.
Must be able to achieve a second class on the final Marine Corps physical fitness test given at Marine Combat Instructor School.
Must be able to achieve a second class on the final Marine Corps combat fitness test given at Marine Combat Instructor School.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements. Complete the Marine Combat Instructor Course (M03U2A4) Camp Lejeune, NC or (M10U2A2) Camp Pendleton, CA.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to Individual Training Standards.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code. Teachers and Instructors, All Other 25-3099.

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Related Military Skill. None.

section.heading: 4. MOS 0914, Marine Special Operations Forces Instructor (MGySgt to Sgt)

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Marine Special Operations Forces Instructors train and certify Marines in entry level or advanced special operations skills. They serve as mentors and coaches, assisting student in the development of problem solving, critical thinking, and cognitive abilities for adaptive decision making. They enable students to master the skills necessary to conduct globally sensitive missions in complex environments.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Must be a sergeant or above.
Mastery of the Marine’s PMOS. 3115 NAVMC 1200.1L 3-93 Enclosure (1)
Must maintain the USMC standards for PFT and CFT for their PMOS.
Must meet Marine Corps height, weight, and body composition standards.
Must meet the prerequisites prescribed in MCO 1553.2C Marine Corps Formal School Management Policy.
Must meet the standards screening checklist of special assignments per MCO 1326.6 Selecting, Screening and Preparing Enlisted Marines for billets and independent duty assignments.
Must possess one of the following primary military occupational specialties (PMOS) 0211, 0231, 0241, 0261, 0372, 0621, 0629, 0631, 0639, 0671, 0679, 0699, 2336, 2629, 2651, 2691, or 2841.
Successful completion of the Special Operations Training Course (M03DTZK), Survival, Evasion, Resistance, Escape Level C Course (M03M47K), and MARSOC Special Operations Force (SOF) Level 1 Training.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements
Must successfully complete the MARSOC Instructor Qualification Course (MO3YEQK) at the Marine Raider Training Center (MRTC) in Camp Lejeune, NC.
Must be appointed in writing as a MRTC Instructor.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties
Trains personnel in entry level and/or advanced special operations skills.
Responsible for the conduct and supervision of high risk training.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code. Teachers and Instructors, All other 25-3099.

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Related Military Skill. None.

section.heading: 5. MOS 0916, Martial Arts Instructor (MGySgt to Cpl) FMOS, CG TECOM

provision.text: MOS 0916, Martial Arts Instructor (MGySgt to Cpl) FMOS, CG TECOM

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Martial Arts Instructors conduct training in principles of close combat and core values.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Must qualify first class on CFT.
Must qualify first class on the PFT.
Must be certified as gray belt or above.
Must have recommendation of reporting senior.
Must be a corporal or above. This prerequisite is non- waiverable. 3115 NAVMC 1200.1L 3-94 Enclosure (1)
Full duty status shoulder injury free in previous 2 years, concussion free within the past 6 months and free of contagious diseases or dermatological conditions.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements
Must complete the appropriate level PME for grade.
Successful completion of the CG TRNGCOM approved Martial Arts Instructor Course (M02MMET).

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties. Trains and certifies personnel from tan through 1st degree black belt.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code. Teachers and Instructors, All Other 25-3099.

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Related Military Skill. Martial Arts Instructor-Trainer, 0917.

section.heading: 6. MOS 0917, Martial Arts Instructor-Trainer (MGySgt to Sgt) FMOS, CG TECOM

provision.text: MOS 0917, Martial Arts Instructor-Trainer (MGySgt to Sgt) FMOS, CG TECOM

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Martial Arts Instructor Trainers train and certify martial arts instructors. Additionally, they provide instruction to all personnel in hand-held weapons, unarmed against hand-held weapons, weapons of opportunity, ground fighting, firearm disarmament, and principles of core values.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Must have recommendation of reporting senior.
Must be certified as a green belt or above in the MCMAP.
Must have completed the appropriate level PME for grade.
Must be sergeant or above. This prerequisite is non-waiverable.
Must qualify with a minimum of first class score on the PFT and CFT.
Must have a minimum of 1 year obligated service upon completion of MAITC.
Full duty status shoulder injury free in previous 2 years, concussion free within the past 6 months and free of contagious diseases or dermatological conditions.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements. Successful completion of the Martial Arts Instructor- Trainer Course (M02MMKT) at The Basic School at Quantico, VA.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties
Trains and certifies personnel in martial arts techniques from tan through 1st degree black belt and trains personnel in martial arts techniques from 2nd through 4th degree black belt.

Trains, certifies, and recertifies martial arts instructors under the CG, TRNGCOM approved Martial Arts Instructor Program of Instruction for Martial Arts Instructors. 3115 NAVMC 1200.1L 3-95 Enclosure (1)

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code. Teachers and Instructors, All Other 25-3099.

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Related Military Skill. Martial Arts Instructor, 0916.

section.heading: 7. MOS 0918, Water Safety/Survival Instructor (MGySgt to Cpl) FMOS, CG TECOM

provision.text: MOS 0918, Water Safety/Survival Instructor (MGySgt to Cpl) FMOS, CG TECOM

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Marine Corps Instructors of water survival train and equip Marines with the requisite knowledge and skills to successfully negotiate water obstacles and survive in emergency situations in aquatic environments. Additionally, they employ water survival skills of increasing levels of ability designed to reduce fear, raise self-confidence, and develop Marines with the ability to survive in water.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Must be the grade of E-4 or above.
Must possess a current 1st class PFT/CFT.
Must complete all aquatic events required by the NAVMC 11627.
Must have at least one year of obligated service time remaining.
Must have a current water survival intermediate swim qualification or higher.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements. Complete one of the CG TRNGCOM approved Marine Corps Instructor of Water Survival Courses (N30L9N1, N30L9NM, M03L9N6, or M03L9NM) at Expeditionary Warfare Training Group Pacific in San Diego, CA or Marine Corps Water Survival School in Camp Lejeune, NC.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties. Responsible for developing, planning, conducting, and supervising Marine Corps Water Survival training and qualifications. For a partial listing of duties and tasks, refer to MCO 1500.52 and NAVMC 3500.33.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code. Teachers and Instructors, All Other 25-3099.

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Related Military Skill. None.

section.heading: 8. MOS 0919, Force Fitness Instructor (MSgt to Sgt) FMOS, CG TECOM

provision.text: MOS 0919, Force Fitness Instructor (MSgt to Sgt) FMOS, CG TECOM

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Assist COs/OICs in development of unit physical training programs that enable accomplishment of mission essential tasks. This includes injury prevention and physical performance enhancement. Assist individual Marines with physical training programs and provide assistance to sports medicine providers in design and execution of fitness programs for Marines returning to duty from injury or extended periods of limited duty.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Must qualify first class PFT.
Must qualify first class on CFT.
Must have recommendation of reporting senior. 3115 NAVMC 1200.1L 3-96 Enclosure (1)
Full duty status: shoulder injury free in previous 2 years, concussion free within the past 6 months and free of contagious diseases of dermatological conditions.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements
Complete the Force Fitness Instructor (FFI) Course (M02MN1T or M02MN1M).

Complete the Physical Fitness Test Monitor Certification Course (FFD01PFT02), the Combat Fitness Test Monitor Certification Course (FFD02CFT02), and the Body Composition Military Appearance Program Monitor Certification Course (FFD03BCP02).
Approval of the commanding officer to whom assigned.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties. For a partial listing of duties and tasks, refer to the Training Military Occupational Specialties Training and Readiness Manual. Otherwise, responsible to manage fitness, MCMAP, and water survival programs, as directed by unit commander.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code. None.

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Related Military Skill. None.

section.heading: 9. MOS 0931, Marksmanship Instructor (MGySgt to Sgt) FMOS *, CG TECOM

provision.text: MOS 0931, Marksmanship Instructor (MGySgt to Sgt) FMOS *, CG TECOM

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Marksmanship Instructors instruct in all phases of the Marine Corps Marksmanship Program on the qualification and requalification on small arms ranges. Additionally, they assist in the operation of firing ranges. This MOS may be assigned to a Marine or used as a billet designator.

provision.label: b.

Must have previously held MOS 0933.
Must be qualified on the service rifle and pistol.

provision.label: c.

provision.text: MOS 0932, Small Arms Weapons Instructor (MGySgt to Sgt) EMOS (0321), CG TECOM

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Small Arms Weapons Instructors conduct all phases of the Marine Corps Marksmanship training. They develop comprehensive marksmanship training plan based on commander's guidance. They conduct and supervise all small arms marksmanship-training evolutions in support of unit mission. This MOS may be assigned to a Marine or used as a billet designator.

Must possess MOS 0933, Marksmanship Coach.
Must be sergeant through gunnery sergeant.
Must have met the MCCS standard for land navigation.
Must have a minimum of six years TIS upon reporting for instruction.
Must have a minimum of one year remaining to EAS upon completion of course.

section.heading: 11. MOS 0933, Marksmanship Coach (Sgt to PFC) FMOS, CG TECOM

provision.text: MOS 0933, Marksmanship Coach (Sgt to PFC) FMOS, CG TECOM

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Marksmanship Coaches analyze difficulties of shooters during dry and live fire exercises in all phases of the Marine Corps Marksmanship Program during qualification and re-qualification. Additionally, they assist in the operation of firing ranges.

Complete MCI 0367A, Marine Marksman. 3115 NAVMC 1200.1L 3-98 Enclosure (1)

section.heading: 12. MOS 0941, Winter Mountain Leader (MGySgt to Sgt) FMOS, CG TECOM

provision.text: MOS 0941, Winter Mountain Leader (MGySgt to Sgt) FMOS, CG TECOM

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. The WML performs duties of the unit mountain leader who is the subject matter expert in mountain warfare tactics, techniques, and procedures (such as over-the-snow mobility and avalanche hazard assessment), acts as an advisor to the commander, and is capable of conducting pre- environment training for their units.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Students must be fit for full duty.
Open to operating force MOSs, sergeant through MGySgt.
Students must have 12 months remaining on service contract.
Students must complete a first class PFT adjusted for altitude on T-1.
Volunteers are recommended due to the intensity level and demanding nature of this training.
Students must have no personal issues (legal, financial, etc.) as this training center is remote and no time will be provided in the course for such issues.
Students must be medically qualified to participate in a demanding physical training program at high altitude (G6PD and sickle cell screened) and be free of chronic or acute orthopedic injuries.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements. Must successfully complete the Winter Mountain Leaders Course (M24M7B1) at the Marine Corps Mountain Warfare Training Center, Bridgeport, CA.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to reference (dj), Mountain Warfare Operations Training and Readiness Manual.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code. None.

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Related Military Skill. None.

provision.text: MOS 0943, Summer Mountain Leader (MGySgt to Sgt) FMOS, CG TECOM

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. The Summer Mountain Leader performs duties of the unit mountain leader who is the subject matter expert in mountain warfare tactics, 3115 NAVMC 1200.1L 3-99 Enclosure (1) techniques, and procedures (such as vertical and horizontal obstacle crossing), acts as an advisor to the commander, and is capable of conducting pre-environment training for their units.

provision.label: b.

Students must be fit for full duty.
Open to combat arms MOSs, sergeant through MGySgt.
Students must have 12 months remaining on service contract.
Volunteers are recommended due to the intensity level and demanding nature of this training.
Students must complete a first class on the physical fitness test within 30 days of reporting and on T-1 adjusted for altitude.
Students must have no personal issues (legal, financial, etc.) as this training center is remote and no time will be provided in the course for such issues.
Students must be medically qualified to participate in a demanding physical training program at high altitude (G6PD and sickle cell screened) and be free of chronic or acute orthopedic injuries.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements. Must successfully complete the Summer Mountain Leaders Course (M24M7A1) at the Marine Corps Mountain Warfare Training Center, Bridgeport, CA.
