Operations and Tactics Instructor (OTI), 0577.
Ground Command and Control (C2) Operations NCO, 8711. 3155 NAVMC 1200.1L 3-504 Enclosure (1) 3155. OCCUPATIONAL FIELD 88, MISCELLANEOUS REQUIREMENT MOS

section.heading: 1. MOS 8870, Special Operations Concepts and Strategy Specialist (MGySgt to

provision.text: MOS 8870, Special Operations Concepts and Strategy Specialist (MGySgt to SSgt) NMOS (0372), DC PP&O

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. The Special Operations Concepts and Strategy Specialists participates in studies and analyses of strategy/policy and complexities within, dynamics of inter/intrastate conflict, historical and comparative perspectives of special operations, WMD proliferation and counter- proliferation, special operations doctrine, concepts, and institutions, crisis management and the contingent use of military power, terrorism, social revolution, and unconventional warfare.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Possess MOS 0372, Critical Skills Operator.
Security requirement: TS/SCI security clearance.
Possess a bachelor’s degree from a college or university that is institutionally accredited by one of the six regional accrediting agencies.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements
Conduct a successful operational deployment in a SOF billet.
Complete one of the following:

provision.label: (a)
provision.text: Naval Postgraduate School (NPS), Defense Analysis, Special Operations and Irregular Warfare (SO/IW) 699 Curriculum, National Defense University (NDU) Joint Special Operations Master of Arts (JSOMA).

provision.label: (b)
provision.text: A graduate degree with course material relevant to special operations, low-intensity conflict, national security and international security.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties

Participates in strategic analysis of past operations and applies historical lessons to future joint and combined operations, in order to discern the relationship between a nation's political interests and goals and the ways military power may be used to achieve them.
Uses knowledge of political, ethnic, and cultural dynamics that explain the outbreak of war between and within modern States.
Uses analytical methods and their application to military modeling, simulations, and gaming.
Provides detailed and conceptual understanding of the development of doctrine for special operations.
Provides detailed understanding of the problems of domestic and international terrorism, social revolution, and other forms of irregular conflict. 3155 NAVMC 1200.1L 3-505 Enclosure (1)

Provides understanding of the political role played by military power in operations short of war, the problems of military crisis management, and the contingent use of force in support of local U.S. policy objectives.
Provides understanding of the likely and potential implications of information warfare on future special operations.
Reviews the historical use of Special Operations Forces, to include how these and similar forces have been organized, trained, equipped, directed, and employed.
Reviews historical and contemporary "small wars" and other forms of low-intensity conflict in Latin America, Asia, and the Middle East.
Performs operational liaison for MAGTF-SOF integration, and with other military and government agencies that conduct Special Operations.
Performs any or all of the above duties and tasks in the realm of Special Operations analysis at top management levels, and research and development activities.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code. None.

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Related Military Skill. None.

section.heading: 2. MOS 8878, Historian (SgtMaj/MGySgt to Sgt) FMOS, CG TECOM

provision.text: MOS 8878, Historian (SgtMaj/MGySgt to Sgt) FMOS, CG TECOM

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Marine Corps Historians function as coordinators of historical activities, including conducting collections, teaching military history, and participating in a military historical writing program of military historical institutions. Primary assignments are to the United States Naval Academy and the Marine Corps History Division.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Must be slated to or assigned to an 8878 historian billet (including field history branch/marine corps historian division).
Must be slated to or assigned as an instructor at the United States Naval Academy teaching history.

Must be slated to or assigned as an instructor at an institution similar to the United States Naval Academy, including professional military education schools and joint/combined/exchange institutions, teaching history.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements
Marines in historian billets should submit credentials to Marine Corps University Marine Corps History Division for assignment of MOS 8878 via their chain of command.

provision.label: (a)
provision.text: Marines who believe they meet intent of the MOS should contact the Director, Marine Corps History Division, for review of credentials.
MOS 8878 will be awarded after 12 successful months in a historian billet as determined by director, marine corps history division. 3155 NAVMC 1200.1L 3-506 Enclosure (1)

Marine reservists belonging to the field history branch/IMA detachment of marine corps history division will complete a managed on-the- job training program overseen by the officer-in-charge of the IMA detachment.

Personnel assigned to the United States Naval Academy or similar institutions as military historians require a masters degree in history or closely aligned discipline with evidence of coursework in military history. Similar institutions may include professional military education schools, undergraduate education institutions, or joint/exchange billets, but the marine must be teaching a military history course.

Marines who previously served successfully in a historian billet will be assigned MOS 8878. Any marine who served in a historian billet but does not see that reflected in their record should contact the director, marine corps history division, for adjudication.
Marines who believe they meet intent of the MOS should contact the Director, Marine Corps History Division, for review of credentials.
Rank waivers will be considered on a case-by-case basis.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties
Researches and writes official histories of marine corps activities.
Supervises, as required, the preparation of such histories with background in historical references, libraries, and archives.
Participates as researcher, interviewer, and editor in oral history interviews with senior officers and key participants insignificant marine corps activities.
Monitors the conduct of oral history interviews by field organizations.
Instructs or may instruct in military history, with emphasis on amphibious warfare, at officer schools.
Prepares lesson plans and supporting instructional material.
Advises commanding officers on historical matters.
Instructs or may instruct in naval service educational institutions such as Command and Staff Colleges or the U.S. service academies.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code. Historian 19-3093.

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Related Military Skill. None. 3156 NAVMC 1200.1L 3-507 Enclosure (1) 3156. OCCUPATIONAL FIELD 89, MISCELLANEOUS REQUIREMENT MOS

section.heading: 1. Introduction. The Command Senior Enlisted Leader Occupational Field is
2. MOS 8910, GCE Marine (MGySgt to Pvt) FMOS, DC PP&O
3. MOS 8911, Billet Designator-Barracks and Grounds Marine (GySgt to Pvt)

provision.text: MOS 8911, Billet Designator-Barracks and Grounds Marine (GySgt to Pvt) FMOS*, DC I&L

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Barracks and Grounds Marines supervise the policing and minor maintenance of barracks and grounds; supervise or assist in the supervision of, training, routine administration; and employment of units.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites. See requirements.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements
Not to be assigned to personnel either as a primary or additional MOS.
To be used only as a billet designator in T/O's.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties
Supervises working parties in maintaining barracks, buildings, and grounds in a clean, sanitary, and orderly condition.
Makes periodic inspections of plumbing, electrical equipment, and other building components and arranges for required repairs.
Maintains a stock of tools, equipment, and housekeeping gear to supply working parties.
Services buildings and materials such as light bulbs and towels.
Performs preventive maintenance and makes minor repairs to tools and equipment. 3156 NAVMC 1200.1L 3-508 Enclosure (1)
Requisitions supplies and equipment.
Accompanies inspecting officer on tours of inspection and prepares reports pertaining to unsanitary or faulty conditions.
Assists in the supervision of a unit engaged in enforcing military regulations and guarding lives and property at a military installation.
Inspects and determines condition of unit weapons and equipment.
Initiates action to correct deficiencies.
Supervises preparation of unit correspondence, reports, schedules, and rosters.
Organizes and supervises the necessary housekeeping functions within the organization.
Conducts or supervises subordinates conducting training in military subjects.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code. Residential Advisors 39-9041.

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Related Military Skill. None.

section.heading: 4. MOS 8972, Aircrew Trainee (GySgt to Pvt) Basic MOS, DC AVN
5. MOS 8991, Sergeant Major of the Marine Corps (SgtMaj) PMOS, DC M&RA

provision.text: MOS 8991, Sergeant Major of the Marine Corps (SgtMaj) PMOS, DC M&RA

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. Assists the CMC as Senior Enlisted Marine in the Marine Corps. Advises the CMC in matters pertaining to enlisted personnel and assists the CMC in the performance of his duties. Performs such specific duties as member of the CMC's enlisted performance board, member of the permanent Marine Corps uniform board, and member of the CMC's party on all visits and inspection trips to Marine Corps installations when enlisted 3156 NAVMC 1200.1L 3-509 Enclosure (1) personnel are involved. When directed by the CMC, assists staff agencies in matters pertaining to enlisted Marines. Represents the CMC at the Staff Noncommissioned Officers symposium.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Possess exemplary qualities of leadership.
Possess to an exemplary degree initiative, sound judgment, industry, and dignity of demeanor.
Possess sufficient training, schooling (formal or OJT) to act independently as principal enlisted assistant in all administrative, technical, and tactical matters in a unit.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements. None.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties
Communicates ideas effectively at all levels.
Possesses to the highest degree the faculty for working in harmony with officers, other noncommissioned officers, and civilians.
Demonstrates a comprehensive understanding of Marine Corps organizations, missions, and staff procedures.
Possesses a comprehensive understanding of staff procedures and inter-organization relationships including inter-service organization and relationships at the highest levels.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code. Human Resources, Training, and Labor Relations Specialists, All Other 13- 1079.

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Related Military Skill. Administrative Specialist, 0111.

section.heading: 6. MOS 8999, Sergeant Major-First Sergeant (SgtMaj to 1stSgt) PMOS, DC M&RA

provision.text: MOS 8999, Sergeant Major-First Sergeant (SgtMaj to 1stSgt) PMOS, DC M&RA

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Summary. The Command Senior Enlisted Leader is responsible to the commander for all matters which effect the morale, welfare, discipline, mission success, and overall readiness of the unit. They disseminate and enforce Marine Corps and local policies, orders, and directives. They possess comprehensive knowledge of Marine Corps organization, history, traditions, customs and courtesies. They are directly responsible for all enlisted career human resource matters within the unit and have a mandate to maintain and develop the total force.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Prerequisites
Security requirement:

provision.label: (a)
provision.text: Top secret clearance required for sergeant major.

provision.label: (b)
provision.text: Secret security clearance required for first sergeant.
Possess a high degree of physical and mental resilience. 3156 NAVMC 1200.1L 3-510 Enclosure (1)
Ability to obtain situational awareness and think critically.
Ability to communicate effectively both orally and in writing.
Demonstrate an ability to multitask and manage shifting priorities.
Must have requested to be considered for 1stSgt on latest fitness report by typing an “F” in item 8h.
Exhibit a consistent and exemplary standard of military appearance, physical fitness, and personal discipline.
Possess a high degree of moral character, ethical standards, embodies our core values, leadership traits and principles.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Requirements
Elected to 1stSgt or SgtMaj by an enlisted promotion board.
1stSgts are required to attend E-8 PME requirements.
1stSgts are required to attend 1stSgt school.
SgtMajs are required to attend E-9 PME requirements.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Duties
1stSgt:

provision.label: (a)
provision.text: Serve as the unit senior enlisted leader (USEL) and subject matter expert to the commander on the responsibilities of command and institutional standards.

provision.label: (b)
provision.text: Communicates commander’s intent and facilitates personnel and professional development.

provision.label: (c)
provision.text: Assist the commander in creating a positive command climate and institutional culture with a focus on readiness, mission, diversity, inclusion, and accountability.

provision.label: (d)
provision.text: Supervise, inspect, and enforce standards relating to good order and discipline, the conduct of drill and ceremonies, military appearance, customs and courtesies.

provision.label: (e)
provision.text: Responsible for the administrative correctness of all enlisted performance evaluations and assists in ensuring the timeliness of the command’s fitness reports and junior enlisted evaluations.

provision.label: (f)
provision.text: Ensures the timely and accurate completion of administrative tasks in support of internal and external correspondence, awards, promotions, MCTFS reporting, and request mast.

provision.label: (g)
provision.text: Disseminate and enforce all applicable orders and policies throughout the organization.

provision.label: (h)
provision.text: Assist in the development and management of professional relationships. 3156 NAVMC 1200.1L 3-511 Enclosure (1)

provision.label: (i)
provision.text: Supervise all personnel matters (i.e. force preservation, quality of life issues, personal and professional development and readiness).

provision.label: (j)
provision.text: Screen personnel within the command for assignment to special duty assignments, screen able “B” billets and overseas assignments.

provision.label: (k)
provision.text: Conduct, supervise and manage enlisted professional education including non-resident and resident PME, unit PME program, annual training requirements and professional reading program.

provision.label: (l)
provision.text: Assist commander in the operational mission of the unit.

provision.label: (m)
provision.text: Assist the commander in the sustainment of unit readiness through all functions of command.

provision.label: (n)
provision.text: Review and advise on legal process’ residing with the unit commander or higher.

provision.label: (o)
provision.text: Assume any additional duties as directed by the commander.
In addition to those duties expected of a 1stSgt, SgtMajs (04 & 05 command level):

provision.label: (a)
provision.text: Fully understand orders, regulations, and doctrinal publications applicable to the command in order to assist the commander in shaping policy.

provision.label: (b)
provision.text: Assist the commander with, retention, career development, retirement and separations of all Marines in the command.

provision.label: (c)
provision.text: Provide oversight and ensure compliance of the unit’s single Marine program.

provision.label: (d)
provision.text: Assist in the mentorship and development of the unit’s enlisted and officers.

provision.label: (e)
provision.text: Provide oversight of the unit’s Prevention Programs and utilization of available services.

provision.label: (f)
provision.text: Assist in the development of staff personnel, special staff, and collateral duty billet holders.

provision.label: (g)
provision.text: Provide oversight of the command inspection program and any external inspections.

provision.label: (h)
provision.text: Assist the Commander with the proper manning and resourcing of personnel throughout subordinate units.

provision.label: (i)
provision.text: Develop, supervise, and train subordinate unit leaders in the proper execution of drill, ceremonies, and protocol.

provision.label: (j)
provision.text: Create professional military education opportunities for Marines within the unit.

provision.label: (k)
provision.text: Assume other duties as designated by the commander and higher headquarters. 3156 NAVMC 1200.1L 3-512 Enclosure (1)
In addition to those duties expected at the 1stSgt and 04/05 level, SgtMajs (06 command level):

provision.label: (a)
provision.text: Interact with higher headquarters in order to advocate for the needs of subordinate units.

provision.label: (b)
provision.text: Interpret and implement higher headquarters policies within mission requirements of subordinate units.

provision.label: (c)
provision.text: Cultivate a positive and non-biased professional relationship and open lines of communication with subordinate command teams.

provision.label: (d)
provision.text: Review and advise on legal process’ unique to commanders with courts martial convening authority.

provision.label: (e)
provision.text: Mentor and develop subordinate unit senior enlisted and commanders and advise on complex unit and personnel challenges.

provision.label: (f)
provision.text: Must be familiar with the titles, authorities, budget, and permissions applicable to the command and its mission.

provision.label: (g)
provision.text: Develop a familiarity with the joint, interagency, intergovernmental, multinational (JIIM) environment and diplomacy, information, military, and economic (DIME) considerations.

provision.label: (h)
provision.text: Assume other duties as designated by the commander and higher headquarter.
In addition to those duties expected at all previous levels, SgtMajs (general/flag officer level):

provision.label: (a)
provision.text: Advise in the development of the command inspection program.

provision.label: (b)
provision.text: Must be well versed in the commanders’ and CMC strategic messaging campaign.

provision.label: (c)
provision.text: Be familiar with strategic level documents (i.e., national defense strategy, national military strategy).

provision.label: (d)
provision.text: Assist the commander with policies affecting DOD civilians and contractors in support of the command.

provision.label: (e)
provision.text: Understanding general officer protocols and professional ethics.

provision.label: (f)
provision.text: Develop a functional understanding of the JIIM environment and DIME/PMESII considerations.

provision.label: (g)
provision.text: Assume other duties as designated by the general officer.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code. None.

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Related Military Skill. None. IMPLEMENTATION OF MOS CONVERSION

section.heading: 1. Deputy Commandant, Manpower and Reserve Affairs

provision.text: Deputy Commandant, Manpower and Reserve Affairs

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Director, Manpower Plans (DC M&RA (MP)). Modify models to reflect MOS changes shown in figure 4-1.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Director, Personnel Management Division (DC M&RA (MM)). Modify models and other supporting information systems to reflect MOS changes shown in figure 4-1. The Type Transaction Code (TTC) conversion for the Marine Corps Total Force System (MCTFS) will convert MOSs (BMOS) and (PMOS) and add requisite non-PMOS (as applicable) for active-duty components. Action will be accomplished by the DC M&RA (MM) on 1 October 2025 to convert the present MOS codes being revised as listed in the table of MOSs to the new MOS codes listed (refer to figure 4-1).

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Director, Management Information Systems Division. Update the MCTFS MOS tables prior to the DC M&RA (MM, RA) submission of the TTC conversions that will occur on 1 October 2025.
Commanding General, Marine Corps Recruiting Command. Ensure MOS conversions are entered into the Marine Corps Recruit Information Support System (MCRISS) on 15 January 2025.

provision.text: Marine Corps Reserve

provision.label: a.
provision.text: DC M&RA (RA). Coordinate retraining of Prior Service MOS Retraining Program” (PSMRP) Marines and Active Reserve (AR) Marines as required for MOS conversion, subject to the availability of funds.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: The Commander, Marine Forces Reserve (COMMARFORRES). Coordinate retraining of SMCR Marines as required for MOS conversion, subject to the availability of funds.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: The Commanding General (CG), Individual Reserve Support Organization (MIRSO). Make appropriate SRB entries for Individual Mobilization Augmentees, Individual Ready Reservists, and Standby Reservists using as authority the DC M&RA (MM) conversion action appearing on the RUC's DFR with an origin of "HQ". NAVMC 1200.1L 4-2 Enclosure (1) 4002. COMMANDING OFFICER'S RESPONSIBILITIES
Active component units verify appropriate conversion actions appearing on the RUC's Diary Feedback Report (DFR) with an origin code of "HQ".
